{{HasStrategy}} {{Infobox Activity |name = Blast mine |image = [[File:Blast mine.png|300px]] |release = [[7 January]] [[2016]] |update = Zeah: Great Kourend |type = Activity |members = Yes |location = [[Lovakengj]] |currency = None |map = {{Map|name=Blast mine|x=1489|y=3864|zoom=2}} |leagueRegion = Kourend }} The '''blast mine''' is an activity which grants [[Mining]] and [[Firemaking]] experience.
Blast mining requires level 43 Mining to participate, as well as a [[chisel]], [[tinderbox]], and [[dynamite]]. Dynamite can be made by combining [[volcanic sulphur]], [[juniper charcoal]], [[saltpetre]], and a [[pot]], then adding a [[ball of wool]] to the resulting [[dynamite pot]]. Alternatively, dynamite can be obtained from [[Thirus]] nearby.
Players use dynamite to blast chunks of valuable [[ores]] from within hard rock, which must then be washed before the chunks disintegrate.
There are bank chests in the area which players can use to retrieve dynamite as needed and to deposit collected ores.
==Transportation== The blast mine is located in the northern section of [[Lovakengj]] and may be accessed via a number of ways:
# Run north from the Xeric's Inferno option on the [[Xeric's talisman]]. # Run north from the [[jewellery of jubilation]] teleport on the [[Kharedst's memoirs]] or [[book of the dead]]. # Run north from Lovakengj station on the [[Lovakengj Minecart Network]].
==Money making== {{Mmgsection|Blast mining|mobname=the blast mine}}
==Gameplay== [[File:Dynamite explosion.png|thumb|The dynamite explodes, blasting rock out of the cavity.]] Players must first excavate hard rock using a [[chisel]], then use a pot of [[dynamite]] on the resulting cavity. Then, they must light the dynamite with a [[tinderbox]] and run at least two squares away from it, or take about 15 damage.
Once the dynamite explodes, players should collect the [[blasted ore]] from the ground and deposit it into an [[ore sack]] near a working [[operator]]. Players have three minutes to deposit the blasted ore before it disintegrates, so it is important to be quick. When there are at least 900 of any single type of ore in the sack, it will become full and the player will need to collect it before being able to excavate any more; the nearby operator will notify them of this. Players can talk to the brown-haired operator on the east side of the machine to collect the ore they mined in noted form, along with [[Mining]] experience according to the ores obtained.
Excavating the hard rock earns 20 [[Mining]] experience, and lighting the dynamite earns 50 [[Firemaking]] experience. Additional Mining experience is awarded along with the cleaned ores.
The blast mine allows players to obtain ores as though their Mining level were 10 levels higher (e.g. a player can obtain [[runite ore]] with only 75 Mining instead of the usual 85). Temporary boosts work, and must be active before the blasted ore spawns. The experience gained per hour varies depending on Mining level and overall efficiency. Additionally, players who have completed the [[elite Kourend & Kebos Diary]] have a 10% increased chance to obtain higher-tier ores.
{| class="wikitable" !Ore !Base experience |- |{{plink|Coal}} |33 |- |{{plink|Gold ore}} |66 |- |{{plink|Mithril ore}} |120 |- |{{plink|Adamantite ore}} |190 |- |{{plink|Runite ore}} |260 |}
Assuming 330 dynamite used per hour, at level 70, players can expect approximately 55,000 Mining experience and 310,000 coins per hour. This scales up to 88,000 and 800,000 respectively at level 99, with the profit increasing significantly at level 75 with runite ore becoming available. In addition, Firemaking experience is gained at 16,500 per hour, which does not scale.
Unlike level boosts, the [[prospector kit]] affects the experience received while collecting the washed ore. It is not required to wear it while blasting ore and depositing blasted ore to obtain the bonus experience. However, the experience of excavating the rock wall is increased by 0.5 experience per excavation with the full outfit.
A breakdown of the ore distribution at level 99 mining with the [[elite Kourend & Kebos Diary]] and a [[celestrial ring]] to provide the invisible +4 mining boost is approximately: {| class="wikitable" |- ! Ore !! Distribution |- | {{plink|Coal}} || 4.5% |- | {{plink|Gold ore}} || 14.3% |- | {{plink|Mithril ore}} || 31.4% |- | {{plink|Adamantite ore}} || 38.6% |- | {{plink|Runite ore}} || 11.2% |}
==Strategy== {{Main|Blast mine/Strategies}} To do blast mining efficiently, it is important to: * Minimise the time wasted waiting for [[dynamite]] to explode. * Minimise the time spent running to and from the deposit sack. * Minimise the amount of damage taken.
These are much easier if a consistent strategy is used. There are many patterns that may be used, with some variation keeping the above points in mind.
Only a [[chisel]] and [[tinderbox]] are required for the activity. A pickaxe is not used, though the special attack of a [[dragon pickaxe]] or higher as well as [[celestial ring]] slightly increase experience and profit.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/Megative3/status/1373790206718058497|date=22 March 2021|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/109241|archivedate=15 March 2023|quote=[Hello! Does Celestial ring +4 mining boost work at Blast mining?] It makes you more likely to get better ore, but doesn't unlock higher-tier ores for you as far as I know.}} [[Graceful outfit]] is highly recommended, and some run energy restoration (such as [[stamina potion]]s) is useful for some patterns as they slowly drain run energy.
==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 8 May 2024 |update = Project Rebalance: Skilling & Poll 81 MTA Changes |change = *The Blast Mine was visually reworked. *Upped XP by ~10% across the board. *The time it takes for blasted ore to despawn was increased from one minute to three minutes. *Ore sack capacity was increased from 450 to 900. *The Kebos Elite Diary now increases your chance to obtain higher-tier ores by 10%. }} {{Subject changes |date = 10 January 2024 |update = Children of the Sun |poll = Varlamore Activities & Kourend Changes |change = The blast mine can now be accessed with only level 43 [[Mining]] as [[Kourend Favour]] has been removed. }} {{Subject changes |date = 23 February 2017 |update = Shift-Click Drop & QoL |poll = Quality of Life - Ten Skilling Suggestions |change = It is now possible to place Dynamite into rock cavities at the blast mine via a left-click option, rather than having to use Dynamite on a cavity. }} {{Subject changes |date = 14 April 2016 |update = Bank Placeholders & PID |poll = |change = A tile of stray blocking in the blast mine has been removed. }} {{Subject changes footer}}
==Trivia== *If the player speaks to the operator about the machine, they will state that it is used to quickly clean the [[blasted ore]]s, and that the design is a secret, with those who try to copy it would "never get it quite right" and that "their machine would break down all the time". This is a reference to the fact that the struts on [[Prospector Percy]]'s water wheel in the [[Motherlode Mine]] often break, while the blast mine's machine never breaks.

To do '''blast mining''' efficiently, it is important to: * Minimise the time wasted waiting for dynamite to explode. * Minimise the time spent running to and from the deposit sack. * Minimise the amount of damage taken.
These are much easier if a consistent strategy is used, following a chosen pattern repeatedly. There are many patterns that may be used, with some variation keeping the above points in mind.
==Requirements== * {{SCP|Mining|43|link=yes}} * [[Chisel]] * [[Tinderbox]] * 1 {{x}} [[dynamite]] for each [[blasted ore]] mined
==Recommended== * High [[Hitpoints]] to sustain several explosions, in case of mistakes
==Setup== {{Recommended equipment |head1={{plink|Graceful hood}}<ref name=run>Improves energy regeneration</ref><ref name=weight>Reduces energy loss</ref> |head2={{plink|Prospector helmet}}<ref name=xp>Increases experience gained</ref> |cape1={{plink|Agility cape}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> / {{plink|Agility cape(t)}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> |cape2={{plink|Graceful cape}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> |cape3={{plink|Spottier cape}}<ref name=weight/> |cape4={{plink|Spotted cape}}<ref name=weight/> |body1={{plink|Graceful top}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> |body2={{plink|Prospector jacket}} / {{plink|Varrock armour 4}}<ref name=xp/> |legs1={{plink|Graceful legs}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> |legs2={{plink|Prospector legs}}<ref name=xp/> |hands1={{plink|Graceful gloves}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> |hands2={{plink|Penance gloves}}<ref name=weight/> |feet1={{plink|Graceful boots}}<ref name=run/><ref name=weight/> |feet2={{plink|Boots of lightness}}<ref name=weight/> |feet3={{plink|Prospector boots}}<ref name=xp/> |ring1={{plink|Celestial ring}}<ref name=boost>Boosts Mining level</ref> / {{plink|Celestial signet}}<ref name=boost/> |special1={{plink|Dragon pickaxe}}<ref name=boost/> / {{plink|Crystal pickaxe}}<ref name=boost/> }}
<references/>
===Inventory=== * Chisel * Tinderbox * Dynamite – multiples of the amount used in one cycle of your chosen pattern * [[Super energy]] or [[stamina potions]] – filling the remaining slots, if losing run energy
It is recommended to equip pieces of the [[prospector kit]] when collecting washed ore from the [[operator]], as the outfit will increase the received experience. It has minimal impact on the experience gained when excavating whilst graceful provides weight reduction. With a high agility level, wearing a mix of prospector and weight reducing gear is enough to sustain run energy.
==Patterns== The following patterns are offered in order of efficiency, measured by the rate of mining blasted ore.
It is recommended to collect washed ore from the [[operator]] only
* when the sack is full * at the end of your trip * when there is enough xp from collecting the ore that it will increasing one's Mining level, which will increase future ore quality
When following these patterns, note that your character can move before the deposit animation is complete, reducing the time it takes to deposit.
===North-west 8-rock=== {{Tile markers box|Module:Tile markers/Blast Mine (NW 8).json}} [[File:New North West Mining pattern.png|right|300px|thumb|The north-western corner of the blast mine; rock tiles numbered for reference]]
This pattern uses the north-west corner, depositing eight blasted ore with each cycle. This pattern is highly efficient but offers little margin for error. This pattern can yield up to 385 blasted ore mined per hour at maximum efficiency, including banking every 3 cycles.{{CiteVideo|author=Sae Bae|title=Blast Mine 2024 - New Efficient Route, Post Update|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pSHyam_7JZw&t=572s|site=YouTube|date=2024-05-13|timestamp=9:32-12:45}}
Using the image as a reference: # Excavate, place, and light dynamite on rock 1 # ''(If repeating)'' Pick up blasted ore from rock 1 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks 2 and 3 # Light dynamite on rocks 2 and 3 # ''(If repeating)'' Pick up blasted ore from rocks 2 and 3 # Excavate, place, and light dynamite on rock 4 # ''(If repeating)'' Pick up blasted ore from rock 4 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks 5 and 6 # Light dynamite on rocks 5 and 6 # ''(If repeating)'' Pick up blasted ore from rocks 5 and 6 # Excavate, place, and light dynamite on rock 7 # ''(If repeating)'' Pick up blasted ore from rock 7 # Excavate, place, and light dynamite on rock 8 # ''(If repeating)'' Pick up blasted ore from rock 8 # ''(If repeating)'' Deposit in the sack # ''(Every 3rd cycle)'' Bank or un-note to withdraw more dynamite and potions # Repeat
The first cycle skips picking up ore and depositing, as the pattern is designed to pick up the ore from the previous cycle. Every cycle after the first will include picking up ore and depositing.
===North-east=== {{Tile markers box|Module:Tile markers/Blast Mine (NE).json}} [[File:Blast mine spots NE.png|right|300px|thumb|The north-eastern corner of the blast mine; tiles marked for reference]]
This pattern uses the north-east corner, depositing 20 blasted ore after 2.5 cycles. This pattern is highly efficient and offers some margin for error. This pattern can yield up to 380 blasted ore mined per hour at maximum efficiency, including banking every 2.5 cycles.{{CiteVideo|author=Sam Ersson RS|title=How To Do The NEW Blast Mine! 100k Mining XP/HR! (Old School Runescape)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cvqljNqkJzA&t=197s|site=YouTube|date=2024-05-09|timestamp=3:17-6:37}}
Using the image as a reference, numbering tiles '''1'''-4 '''right'''-left: # ''(If ore is ready)'' Pick up blasted ore on tile 1 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 1 # Light dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 1 # ''(If ore is ready)'' Pick up blasted ore on tile 2 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 2 # Light dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 2 # ''(Every 5 cycles, starting at 2.5)'' ## Pick up blasted ore on tiles 3, 4, 2, 1, in that order ## Deposit in the sack ## Bank or un-note to withdraw more dynamite and potions # ''(If ore is ready)'' Pick up blasted ore on tile 3 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 3 # Light dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 3 # ''(If ore is ready)'' Pick up blasted ore on tile 4 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 4 # Light dynamite on rocks adjacent to tile 4 # ''(Every 5 cycles, starting at 5)'' ## Pick up blasted ore on tiles 1, 2, 3, 4, in that order<!-- The cited video did not cover the order for the 5th cycle pickup --> ## Deposit in the sack ## Bank or un-note to withdraw more dynamite and potions # Repeat
This pattern can be altered to deposit and bank every 2.75 cycles, providing increased efficiency{{fact|how much?}} and no margin for error.
===North-west 6-rock=== {{Tile markers box|Module:Tile markers/Blast Mine (NW 6).json}} [[File:Blast mine spots.png|right|300px|thumb|The north-western corner of the blast mine; rocks numbered for reference]]
This pattern uses the north-west corner, depositing six blasted ore with each cycle. This pattern offers ample time to move to the next spot to avoid damage, and picking up the ore often allows for extended breaks. This pattern can yield up to 362 blasted ore mined per hour at maximum efficiency, including banking every 4 cycles. <!-- Calculation: (Ticks per hour / ticks per inventory) × dynamite per inventory ((60×100) / (ticks per cycle × 4 + additional ticks spent when banking between deposit and rock 1)) × 24 ((60×100) / (98×4 + 5)) × 24 362.7204030 -->
Using the image as a reference: # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks 1 and 2 # Light dynamite on rocks 1 and 2 # Excavate and place dynamite on rock 3 # Excavate and place dynamite on rock 4 # Light dynamite on rock 4 # Light dynamite on rock 3 # Excavate and place dynamite on rocks 5 and 6 # Light dynamite on rocks 5 and 6 # Pick up blasted ore from rocks 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 6, in that order # Deposit in the sack # ''(Every 4th cycle)'' Bank to withdraw more dynamite and potions # Repeat
With perfect timing, you will arrive at rock 3 at the same time that it regenerates.

{{Infobox Item |name = Blasted ore |image = [[File:Blasted ore.png]] |release = [[7 January]] [[2016]] |update = Zeah: Great Kourend |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = No |bankable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine = It needs washing before it disintegrates. |value = 60 |weight = 2.267 |id = 13575 }} [[File:Blasted ore detail.png|left|120px]] '''Blasted ore''' is obtained after detonating a hard rock face in the [[blast mine]]. Players must first excavate the hard rock using a [[chisel]], then using a pot of [[dynamite]] on the resulting cavity. Then, players must light the dynamite and run away from it, or large amounts of damage will be taken.
Once the dynamite explodes, blasted ore will appear where the dynamite exploded. It should then be deposited in an ore sack near a blonde-haired [[operator]]. Players have three minutes before the blasted ore disintegrates, so it is encouraged to deposit the ore frequently.
Should the player pick up but not deposit the blasted ore in the Ore sack in time, the blasted ore will disappear from the inventory and a message will appear in the chat interface "Your blasted ore has disintegrated." Hopping worlds will also cause all blasted ore to disintegrate.
If a temporary boost is to be applied when blast mining, they must be activated before the blasted ore is initially spawned.
Like [[pay-dirt]], blasted ore cannot be deposited in a [[bank]].

{{External|dw}} [[File:Bleed hitsplat.png|left]] [[File:Bleeding player.png|thumb|A player taking damage over time from bleeding.]] '''Bleed''' is a temporary status effect that causes the player to lose a set amount of [[hitpoints]] over a short time. Players who are bleeding will be dealt three hitpoints of damage every three ticks. * Bleed inflicted by custodian stalkers causes the player to lose 9 Hitpoints over 9 seconds (15 ticks). However, if the player is moving, they will take damage every tick. * Bleed inflicted by Vardorvis causes the player to lose 15 hitpoints over 8.4 seconds (14 ticks) if the player is standing still. However, if the player is moving, they will take damage every tick, causing them to lose a total of 42 hitpoints instead.
Currently, only [[Vardorvis]], the [[Emissary Enforcer]] and [[custodian stalker]]s (including [[Strange creature (Shadows of Custodia)|strange creatures]], their quest variant) are capable of inflicting bleed on players. However, [[Zebak]]'s melee attack uses a similar mechanic.
Bleed can be cured by applying a [[haemostatic dressing]], which also heals 5 [[Hitpoints]].

Blessed Dizana's quiver is an upgraded variant of Dizana's quiver, made by using it on a Shrine of Ralos while having a total of 150,000 sunfire splinters in the player's inventory and in the quiver. Charging the quiver with sunfire splinters contributes to the required amount of splinters to upgrade.

It's been blessed by Ralos. |examine2 = A quiver awarded to those who have proved their worth in the Colosseum. It's been blessed by Ralos. |examine3 = A broken Quiver awarded to those who have proved their worth in the Colosseum. Blessed by Ralos. |value = 100000 |weight = 0.453 |id1 = 28955 |id2 = 28957 |id3 = 28828 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Blessed dizana's quiver detail.png|150px|left]] |version2 = [[File:Blessed dizana's quiver (l) detail.png|left|150px]] |version3 = [[File:Blessed dizana's quiver (broken) detail.png|150px|left]] }} '''Blessed Dizana's quiver''' is an upgraded variant of [[Dizana's quiver]], made by using it on a [[Shrine of Ralos]] while having a total of 150,000 [[sunfire splinters]] and a Dizana's quiver in the player's inventory. Charging the quiver with sunfire splinters contributes to the required amount of splinters to upgrade. The blessed quiver permanently gains the effects of ''Dizana's Sunfire'', where an additional +1 [[Ranged Strength]] and +10 [[Ranged accuracy]] is applied to stored [[arrows]] and [[bolts]] - essentially acting as a variant of the original with unlimited charges. The upgraded variant also retains its level 75 [[Ranged]] requirement to equip. It can also be combined with the [[max cape]] to change its appearance by turning it into [[Dizana's max cape]]. [[File:Blessed dizana's quiver interface.png|thumb|The quiver's interface when opening it]] ==Combat stats== {{Infobox Bonuses |version1 = Normal |version2 = Locked |version3 = Broken |astab = 0 |aslash = 0 |acrush = 0 |amagic = 0 |arange = +18 |dstab = 0 |dslash = 0 |dcrush = 0 |dmagic = 0 |drange = 0 |str = 0 |rstr = +3 |mdmg = 0 |prayer = 0 |slot = cape |image = [[File:Blessed dizana's quiver equipped male.png|130px]] |altimage = [[File:Blessed dizana's quiver equipped female.png|130px]] }} ==Upgrading== Players can bring the quiver to [[Ava]], along with [[Ava's assembler]], [[Ava's accumulator]], or their [[max cape]] equivalents, to apply the same ammunition-saving effect of her devices to the quiver. Doing so will '''not''' consume the devices. Upgrading the quiver with the [[ranging cape]] will only provide the effect of Ava's accumulator; the quiver must be combined with Ava's assembler to receive its effect. This upgrade applies to '''all''' quivers the player owns, now and in the future - if a player loses all of their quivers and obtains a new one, they will '''not''' need to go back to Ava to reobtain the ammo-saving effect. The interaction between Ava devices and metal torsos '''does not''' carry over when adding the Ava effects to the Dizana's quiver. Blessing the quiver retains any ammo-saving effects used on an unblessed [[Dizana's quiver]]. ==Wilderness== If the player dies below level 20 [[Wilderness]], it will remain in the player's inventory, but will be unusable and require {{NoCoins|400000|c}} to repair. The killer will receive {{NoCoins|400000|c}} as well as any ammo that the quiver was holding, though any sunfire charges will not be lost. Above level 20 Wilderness, a lesser amount will be dropped, along with any ammo in the quiver; the quiver itself and its charges will be destroyed in the process. The quiver - along with its [[Dizana's max cape|max cape variant]] - can be locked by bringing it, along with a [[Trouver parchment|Trouver Parchment]] and {{Coins|500,000}}, to [[Perdu]]. This will allow the quiver to be kept upon death to another player above 20 wilderness. ==Creation== {{Recipe |members = Yes |ticks = 0 |facilities = Shrine of Ralos |mat1 = Dizana's quiver |mat1cost = No |mat2 = Sunfire splinters |mat2quantity = 150000 |output1 = Blessed dizana's quiver |output1cost = No }} ==Products== {{Uses material list|Blessed dizana's quiver}} ==Used in recommended equipment== {{Used in recommended equipment|Dizana's quiver|Blessed dizana's quiver}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 17 April 2024 |update = Undead Pirates Tweaks, Varlamore CAs & More |change = The item has been [[graphically updated]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Blessed dizana's quiver detail v1.png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Blessed dizana's quiver detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Blessed dizana's quiver v1.png|center]] |[[File:Blessed dizana's quiver.png|center]] |- |20 March 2024 –

{{External|rs|rsc=Blessed Golden Bowl}} {{Infobox Item |name = Blessed gold bowl |image = [[File:Blessed gold bowl.png]] |release = [[20 August]] [[2003]] |update = New - Legends Quest! |members = Yes |quest = [[Legends' Quest]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine = A specially-made bowl constructed out of pure gold and blessed by Gujuo. |value = 700 |weight = 0.800 |id = 722 }} [[File:Blessed gold bowl detail.png|left|170px]] The '''blessed gold bowl''' is a [[quest item]] made during or after the [[Legends' Quest]]. It is described by [[Gujuo]] as a bowl made of the metal of the sun. The player must make the gold bowl by using two [[gold bar]]s and a [[hammer]] at an anvil while holding the [[sketch]] given to the player by Gujuo to make a [[gold bowl]]. The bowl can then be taken back to Gujuo to be blessed (must have 42 prayer points, however they will not be consumed), to make it ready for it to hold the holy water needed to free [[Ungadulu]]. It is possible to fail when blessing the bowl causing the player to lose 5 prayer points in the process. If the blessed bowl is filled with the sacred pure water of the [[Kharazi Jungle|Kharazi]] water pool, it becomes a [[golden bowl]] containing sacred pure water that can be used with an [[enchanted vial]] to make a vial of [[holy water]]: one bowl can fill up to 10 vials. After making one successful golden bowl, the player can smith a gold bowl at any anvil, without need of the sketch, for 30 [[Smithing]] experience (though there remains a chance of failure); the bowl can then be taken to Gujuo to have it blessed. '''Note:''' Filling an unblessed gold bowl from the Kharazi water pool will also create a golden bowl, but the examine information will reveal that the water is pure but no longer sacred. Filling a gold bowl or a blessed bowl with plain water from some other water source results in only plain water. ==Creation== {{Recipe |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} Partial completion of [[Legends' Quest]] |skill1 = Prayer |skill1lvl = 42 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 0 |members = Yes |ticks = 25 |facilities = Gujuo |mat1 = Gold bowl |mat1cost = No |output1 = Blessed gold bowl |output1cost = No }} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 30 January 2006 |update = Runesquares, Harpie Bugs and new potato recipes! |change = The item was graphically updated. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Blessed gold bowl detail (historical).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Blessed gold bowl detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Blessed gold bowl (historical).png|center]] |[[File:Blessed gold bowl.png|center]] |- |29 March 2004 ⁠–

{{external|rs}} {{Infobox Item |version1 = Empty |version2 = Blood |version3 = Garlic |version4 = Spices |version5 = Complete |name = Blessed pot |image1 = [[File:Blessed pot (empty).png]] |image2 = [[File:Blessed pot (blood).png]] |image3 = [[File:Blessed pot (garlic).png]] |image4 = [[File:Blessed pot (spice).png]] |image5 = [[File:Blessed pot (complete).png]] |release = [[18 April]] [[2005]] |update = Desert Treasure |members = Yes |quest = [[Desert Treasure I]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine1 = A silver pot made by Ruantun and blessed on Entrana. |examine2 = A blessed silver pot made by Ruantun filled with your blood. |examine3 = A blessed silver pot filled with blood and garlic. |examine4 = A blessed silver pot filled with blood and spices. |examine5 = A blessed silver pot filled with blood, garlic and spices. |value = 250 |weight = 0.453 |id1 = 4659 |id2 = 4661 |id3 = 4663 |id4 = 4667 |id5 = 4665 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Blessed pot (empty) detail.png|left|150x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Blessed pot (blood) detail.png|left|150x150px]] |version3 = [[File:Blessed pot (garlic) detail.png|left|150x150px]] |version4 = [[File:Blessed pot (spice) detail.png|left|150x150px]] |version5 = [[File:Blessed pot (complete) detail.png|left|150x150px]] }} The '''blessed pot''' is a quest item created by taking a [[silver pot (Desert Treasure I)|silver pot]] made by [[Ruantun]] to be blessed by the [[High Priest (Entrana)|High Priest]] on [[Entrana]].
Talking to [[Malak]] will let him damage you for 5 [[hitpoints]], filling the pot with blood. Spices and garlic must then be added (in either order) to complete it, after which it can be used to summon [[Dessous]]. If the player has 5 or less hitpoints, he will do damage that leaves at least 1 hitpoint. It should also be noted that even if the player has one hitpoint, he will instead hit a zero and the player will still obtain a pot with their blood.
After the player completes their task from Malak and collects the [[blood diamond]], he will confiscate the pot (all variants) from the player's inventory or bank. Should the player wish to keep it or a copy, they should drop it before speaking to Malak. If the player loses the blood diamond and reclaims it from him, he will again confiscate any blessed pots the player may have in their possession.
{{Desert Treasure I}}

Like most spiders, blessed spiders attack with [[melee]] and are weak to [[crush]]. Blessed spiders are initially not [[aggressiveness|aggressive]] to players with a combat level of 78 or above. However, if Kalrag is killed, they become aggressive to players of all levels, and are able to attack the player simultaneously as if they were in a [[multicombat area]]. {{Infobox Item |name = Blessed superior dragon bones |image = [[File:Blessed superior dragon bones.png]] |release = [[20 March]] [[2024]] |update = Varlamore: Part One |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Break-down, Drop |examine = Bones blessed at an exposed altar. |value = 160 |weight = 1.800 |id = 29362 }} [[File:Blessed superior dragon bones detail.png|130px|left]] '''Blessed superior dragon bones''' are the blessed form of [[superior dragon bones]] obtained by using them on the [[exposed altar]] on the summit of [[Ralos' Rise]]. They are broken down with a [[chisel]] to obtain 121 [[blessed bone shards]] and 5 [[Crafting]] experience, which can then be sacrificed at the [[libation bowl]] at [[the Teomat]].
Unlike other types of blessed bones, blessed superior dragon bones require a [[Prayer]] level of 70 to be blessed at the exposed altar.
As each shard sacrificed gives 5 [[Prayer]] experience, each blessed bone gives 605 Prayer experience overall. If using a [[jug of blessed sunfire wine]] at the libation bowl instead of a regular [[jug of blessed wine]], this is increased to 6 Prayer experience per shard, or 726 Prayer experience per bone.
Players looking to bless bones in bulk may talk to [[Virilis]], found at the base of the exposed altar, to unnote any type of [[bones]] for a fee of 10 [[coins]] per bone.

revision.text:
{{Deadman permanent}} {{Infobox Item |defver = 4 |version1 = 1 dose |version2 = 2 dose |version3 = 3 dose |version4 = 4 dose |bucketname1 = (1) |bucketname2 = (2) |bucketname3 = (3) |bucketname4 = (4) |name1 = Blighted overload (1) |name2 = Blighted overload (2) |name3 = Blighted overload (3) |name4 = Blighted overload (4) |image1 = [[File:Blighted overload (1).png]] |image2 = [[File:Blighted overload (2).png]] |image3 = [[File:Blighted overload (3).png]] |image4 = [[File:Blighted overload (4).png]] |release = [[17 July]] [[2024]] |update = Deadman: Armageddon & While Guthix Sleeps Updates |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Drink, Empty, Drop |examine1 = 1 dose of blighted overload potion. |examine2 = 2 doses of blighted overload potion. |examine3 = 3 doses of blighted overload potion. |examine4 = 4 doses of blighted overload potion. |value = 50 |weight1 = 0.020 |weight2 = 0.025 |weight3 = 0.030 |weight4 = 0.035 |exchange = dmm |id1 = 29640 |id2 = 29637 |id3 = 29634 |id4 = 29631 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Blighted overload (1) detail.png|left|120px]] |version2 = [[File:Blighted overload (2) detail.png|left|120px]] |version3 = [[File:Blighted overload (3) detail.png|left|120px]] |version4 = [[File:Blighted overload (4) detail.png|left|120px]] }} '''Blighted overloads''' are a stat-boosting potion exclusive to [[Deadman Mode]]. Although they are listed in the [[Grand Exchange]] in all [[Members world|members worlds]], they remain an unobtainable item outside of Deadman worlds. Players can make this potion at level 83 [[Herblore]] by combining a 4-dose [[super combat potion]], [[ranging potion]], and [[magic potion]] with a piece of [[chitin]], which are obtained from killing monsters at a [[breach]]. A dose of blighted overload, which can only be drunk in dangerous areas, will boost the player's offensive skills, reduce the player's Defence, and cause the player to take 10 damage over the course of 6 seconds (2 damage every 2 ticks). The stat boosts are re-applied every 15 seconds for five minutes until the effects wear off; for Defence, the level will decay if it is over 90% of the player's base level. The blighted overload effect will be removed if the player goes into a safezone with the effect active for longer than 11 ticks. {{Bug|Blighted overloads appear on the Grand Exchange in main game worlds.}} ==Effects== ===Attack & Strength Boost=== Attack and Strength boost is calculated by:

\lfloor 0.15 \times \text{Level} \rfloor + 8

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !{{SCP|Attack}} {{SCP|Strength}} Level!!Boost!!{{SCP|Attack}} {{SCP|Strength}} Level!!Boost!!{{SCP|Attack}} {{SCP|Strength}} Level!!Boost |- |'''1-6'''||+8||'''34-39'''||+13||'''67-73'''||+18 |- |'''7-13'''||+9||'''40-46'''||+14||'''74-79'''||+19 |- |'''14-19'''||+10||'''47-53'''||+15||'''80-86'''||+20 |- |'''20-26'''||+11||'''54-59'''||+16||'''87-93'''||+21 |- |'''27-33'''||+12||'''60-66'''||+17||'''94-99'''||+22 |} ===Defence Drain=== Defence drain is calculated by:

\lfloor \frac{\text{Level}}{10} \rfloor + 1

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !{{SCP|Defence}} Level!!Boost!!{{SCP|Defence}} Level!!Boost |- |'''1-10'''||-1||'''51-60'''||-6 |- |'''11-20'''||-2||'''61-70'''||-7 |- |'''21-30'''||-3||'''71-80'''||-8 |- |'''31-40'''||-4||'''81-90'''||-9 |- |'''41-50'''||-5||'''91-99'''||-10 |} ===Ranged Boost=== Ranged boost is calculated by:

\lfloor \frac{\text{Level}}{10} \rfloor + 7

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !{{SCP|Ranged}} Level!!Boost!!{{SCP|Ranged}} Level!!Boost |- |'''1-9'''||+7||'''50-59'''||+12 |- |'''10-19'''||+8||'''60-69'''||+13 |- |'''20-29'''||+9||'''70-79'''||+14 |- |'''30-39'''||+10||'''80-89'''||+15 |- |'''40-49'''||+11||'''90-99'''||+16 |} ===Magic Boost=== Magic boost is calculated by:

\lfloor \frac{\text{Level}}{10} \rfloor + 1

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !{{SCP|Magic}} Level!!Boost!!{{SCP|Magic}} Level!!Boost |- |'''1-9'''||+1||'''51-60'''||+6 |- |'''11-20'''||+2||'''61-70'''||+7 |- |'''21-30'''||+3||'''71-80'''||+8 |- |'''31-40'''||+4||'''81-90'''||+9 |- |'''41-50'''||+5||'''91-99'''||+10 |} ==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Herblore |skill1lvl = 83 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 125 |members = Yes |ticks = 2 |mat1 = Super combat potion(4) |mat2 = Ranging potion(4) |mat3 = Magic potion(4) |mat4 = Chitin |output1 = Blighted overload (4) }} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 21 January 2026 |update = Holy Moleys and the Hooded Slayer Helm are Here! |change = * Blighted overloads deal 10 damage, down from 25. * Defence level now decays down to 90% of its original value, up from 80%. }} {{Subject changes |date = 12 March 2025 |update = Permanent Deadman: World 345 Improvements |change = Players can now create blighted overloads on the permanent Deadman world. }} {{Subject changes footer}} {{Deadman Mode}} {{Deadman: Annihilation}} {{Deadman: Armageddon}} {{Blighted items}}

'''Blighted rune sacks''' are [[blighted]] items that allow the player to cast the respective spell without needing any runes and are significantly cheaper to use. However, they can only be used in the [[Wilderness]], [[Ferox Enclave]], [[Mage Arena bank]], [[PvP world]]s, [[Castle Wars]], [[Clan Wars]], and [[Soul Wars]].
They can be bought from [[Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing]], [[Soul Wars Reward Shop]], [[Emir's Arena]] and dropped by [[revenants]].
Types of blighted stacks:
* [[Blighted ancient ice sack]] * [[Blighted bind sack]] (historical) * [[Blighted entangle sack]] * [[Blighted snare sack]] (historical) * [[Blighted surge sack]] * [[Blighted teleport spell sack]] * [[Blighted vengeance sack]] * [[Blighted wave sack]] (historical)
{{Disambig}}

{{Infobox Combat Achievement |name = Blind Spot |image = [[File:Tekton.png|220px]] |release = [[21 July]] [[2021]] |update = Combat Achievements |members = Yes |description = Kill Tekton without taking any damage. |tier = Master |monster = Chambers of Xeric |type = Perfection |id = 319 |leagueRegion = Kourend }} '''Blind Spot''' is a [[Combat Achievements/Master|master combat achievement]] which requires the player to kill [[Tekton]] without taking any damage.
==Strategy== You do not need to receive kill credit for Tekton in order to complete this achievement. So it is easiest to get a partner to tank him and do most of the damage while you land one damaging hit. In order to speed up the kill you can have the partner stand on the opposite side of Tekton and hit him only right after he swings at your partner then walk away like you would at guardians.
Lure Tekton to the centre of the arena, away from any pillars of smoke, as these have erratic hitboxes and can deal 1-3 damage when standing on them, disqualifying them from the achievement. Use one of the flinching or running methods to avoid Tekton's standard attacks. Be careful of the fireballs launched during his repair state as they have a 3x3 AoE; while they should generally hit together, they may occasionally desync and hit on different ticks due to travel distance.
Unlike other cox combat achievements, you need to be in the room at the end of the fight to complete the achievement. Entering through Tekton's fire will fail the achievement, meaning the player must be present the whole fight.
'''For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.'''
==Other tasks== {{Combat Achievements list|Chambers of Xeric}}
{{Combat Achievements}}

revision.text:
{{External|rs=Blood altar}} {{otheruses|the true altar in the [[Meiyerditch Laboratories]]|the recreated altar in [[Great Kourend]]|Blood Altar (Kourend)}} {{Infobox Scenery |name = Altar |image = [[File:Altar (blood).png|300px]] |release = [[23 March]] [[2022]] |update = Guardians of the Rift Launch |aka = True Blood Altar |members = Yes |quest = [[Sins of the Father]] |location = [[Meiyerditch Laboratories]] |options = Craft-rune |examine = A mysterious power emanates from this shrine. |map = {{Map|mtype=pin|x = 3231|y = 4831|mapID=-1}} |id = 43479 |leagueRegion = Morytania }} The '''Blood Altar''' (or '''true Blood Altar''') is a [[runic altar]] used to craft [[blood rune]]s from [[pure essence]]. Crafting blood runes at this altar provides 10.5 [[Runecraft]] [[experience]] per essence imbued. Level 77 [[Runecraft]] and completion of the [[quest]] [[Sins of the Father]] is required to craft blood runes.
Players may create a [[blood tiara]] here by using either a [[blood talisman]] or a [[tiara]] on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 52.5 [[Runecraft]] [[experience]]. A [[catalytic tiara]] can also be created here by using a [[catalytic talisman]] and [[gold tiara]], granting 42.5 Runecraft experience.
A second [[Blood Altar (Kourend)|Blood Altar]] exists in [[Great Kourend]]. It was created by the power from the [[Dark Altar]] located near it, which draws energy from the plane where the true Blood Altar is located. Kourend's Blood Altar does not require a [[blood talisman]] to access.
==Transportation== [[File:Blood Altar non-Abyss route.png|thumb|left|280px|Routes to the Blood Altar via the Myreque Hideout.]] The Blood Altar can be accessed from the trapdoor behind the [[Hair of the Dog]] tavern in [[Canifis]] or via [[fairy ring]] code {{fairycode|DLS}}, requiring [[In Search of the Myreque]], to be completed for quicker access to the hideout. Enter the cavern containing the tomb of Ivandis and take the other exit to arrive at the end of the [[Meiyerditch Laboratories]]. Players with level 74 [[Agility]] can access a [[Cave (Meiyerditch Laboratories medium)|shortcut]] at the end of the first path that takes them to the altar's entrance.
Players with level 93 [[Agility]] and 78 [[Mining]], both of which can be [[boost]]ed, can access a [[Cave (Meiyerditch Laboratories advanced)|superior shortcut]] directly from the southern end of the [[Myreque Hideout]] from the tavern that takes them to west of the chamber containing the altar's entrance. However, players must mine their way through the strange wall in the laboratory tunnels to permanently unlock access to it.
To enter the mysterious ruins, players either have to use a [[blood talisman]] on the ruins, or click "Enter" on the ruins while wearing a [[blood tiara]]. Alternatively, a [[catalytic talisman]] or [[catalytic tiara|tiara]] can be used.
The Blood Altar can also be reached via the [[Abyss]]; the [[blood rift]] within the abyss is directed to both the true Blood Altar in [[Morytania]] and the [[Blood Altar (Kourend)|false altar]] in [[Kourend]].
==Strategy== {{Inventory |align = right|Quest point cape (t)|Colossal pouch|Blood essence (active)|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence|Pure essence| }} For high-level true Blood Altar runs while not using the [[Abyss]], the following is recommended: a fairy ring teleport (such as the [[quest point cape]]), an equipable bank teleport (such as the [[Crafting cape]]), the [[colossal pouch]], and completion of [[Lunar Diplomacy]] for the [[NPC Contact]] spell to periodically repair the pouch. Players should also have a steady supply of [[stamina potions]] to restore their run energy; a [[ring of endurance]] extends time between potion usages significantly. Those with a [[Runecraft cape]] may wish to use an [[Enchanted Lyre(i)]] or other non-cape teleport in order to prevent essence pouches from degrading.
The optimal setup is as follows:
* [[Construct. cape|Construction Cape]]: fairy ring teleport in one's POH
* Crafting cape or other equipable bank teleport
* Colossal Pouch
* Access to the NPC Contact spell
* Full [[Raiments of the Eye|Raiments of the Eye outfit]]
* Blood essence
==Money making== {{Mmgsection|Crafting blood runes}}
==Products== {{Uses facility list|Blood Altar, Catalytic runic altar}}
==Gallery== <gallery mode="packed" heights="160"> Meiyerditch Laboratories - true Blood Altar entrance.png|The entrance to the Blood Altar. Blood Altar location.png|The inside of the Blood Altar. </gallery>
==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |update = Guardians of the Rift Launch |poll = Old School Content Poll 76: Game Improvements |date = 23 March 2022 |change = * The true Blood Altar was made accessible. * The pre-existing delay after using Essence on Runecraft Altars was removed.
}} {{Subject changes |update = Darkmeyer |date = 4 June 2020 |change = The ruins leading to the true Blood Altar were added to the game, but the altar itself remained inaccessible. }} {{Subject changes footer}}
==Trivia== [[File:Blood Altar - Dark Altar connection.png|thumb|200px|The giant blood crystal from which the Dark Altar draws the energy to create Kourend's Blood Altar. Jovan's corpse can be seen next to it.]] * At the Blood Altar, a giant crystal can be seen discharging energy upwards. This is where the [[Dark Altar]] draws the energy used to create Kourend's [[Blood Altar (Kourend)|Blood Altar]]. * Examining the skeleton in front of the aforementioned crystal results in the text "A message carved into the ground next to it reads: 'Minas, I'm sorry.'" ** This skeleton belongs to a miner named Jovan, who went mad after coming into contact with a [[blood talisman]] during excavations in the Meiyerditch Laboratories, and subsequently stabbed Minas, who wrote the [[Tatty note (Sins of the Father)|tatty note]] that can be found by searching his skeleton. ** The note contains a request to block the entrance to the altar once more as it is too dangerous, making it possible the altar itself is a corrupting influence. * On the western and eastern side of the Blood Altar, players can use the [[oculus orb]] to view inaccessible templates of the [[Drill Demon]] [[random event]] area and [[Clan Wars]], respectively. This is because the Blood Altar, like all areas not on the overworld map, is actually located on a section of the world map above the [[Wilderness]] which houses all of the underground and other non-surface areas of the game. Drill Demon and Clan Wars [[instances]] are generated from the templates seen via the Blood Altar. * In ''RuneScape 3'', the Blood Altar was released on 22 April 2008 alongside {{RSL|Legacy of Seergaze}}. Although the mysterious ruins leading to the true Blood Altar were added to ''Old School'' on 4 June 2020 when Sins of the Father was released, it was not made accessible at the time due to the false Blood Altar already existing in Kourend. It was made accessible on 23 March 2022 alongside the addition of the blood talisman as a reward from the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[Temple Supplies|reward shop]]. * Upon entering the true Blood Altar, the [[music]] track [[Bloodbath]] plays. This was the same music track used for ''RuneScape 3''{{'}}s Blood Altar in 2008; in ''Old School'' it was also used for the [[Slepe]] area. * Inside the altar, the shape of the main island is a blood drop, which bears the same symbol as the one on the [[blood rune]].
{{Runecraft}}

{{External|rs}} {{Otheruses|the diamond from the Desert Treasure I quest|the Ancient Sceptre upgrade item|Blood quartz}} {{Infobox Item |name = Blood diamond |image = [[File:Blood diamond.png]] |release = [[18 April]] [[2005]] |update = Desert Treasure |members = Yes |quest = [[Desert Treasure I]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine = The Diamond of Blood. |value = 250 |alchable = 150 |weight = 0.001 |id = 4670 }} [[File:Blood diamond detail.png|left|150px]] The '''blood diamond''' is one of four [[Diamonds of Azzanadra]] obtained during the [[Desert Treasure I]] [[quest]]. It is obtained by defeating [[Dessous]] and then talking to [[Malak]] who will give the player the diamond.
It is recommended that players deposit this gem in the bank as soon as they obtain it, along with the other Diamonds of Azzanadra, as a level 95 [[stranger]] may appear and attack them if they are holding one of them. The more diamonds you have on you, the more likely the stranger will appear and attack you.
Should the player lose the diamond or want to collect another via [[drop trick]], speaking to Malak will allow another one to be obtained. However, all variants of the [[Silver pot (Desert Treasure I)|silver]] or [[blessed pot]] will be taken from the player and the only way to avoid this is dropping them. To keep a copy of the diamond after the quest, drop a duplicate before putting the last Diamond of Azzanadra into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk and it will be safely kept afterwards, even upon quest completion.
{{Desert Treasure I}} {{Gems}}

revision.text:
{{External|rs|rsc=Blood-Rune}} {{Infobox Item |name = Blood rune |image = [[File:Blood rune.png]] |release = [[18 March]] [[2002]] |update = Latest RuneScape News (18 March 2002) |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = Yes |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine = Used for high level missile spells. |value = 400 |weight = 0.000 |respawn = 200 |exchange = Yes |id = 565 }} [[File:Blood rune detail.png|left|120px]] '''Blood runes''' are one of the [[runes]] used to cast spells in the [[Magic]] skill. They are used in some of the highest level spells, the lowest of which is [[Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Ruby)|Ruby Crossbow Bolt Enchant]], and the highest is [[Heal Group]]. Blood runes are also used in charging the [[Scythe of Vitur]], [[Sanguinesti staff]], [[Ring of shadows]], and [[soul bearer]]. ==Runecraft info== Crafting blood runes at one of the two available [[runic altar]]s requires 77 [[Runecraft]]. A [[Blood essence]] can be activated to provide a 50% chance per essence or fragment crafted to produce an extra blood rune. It is consumed and will disappear after 1,000 extra blood runes are crafted. The [[Blood Altar (Kourend)|false Blood Altar]] north of [[Arceuus]] has no quest requirements to use and does not require any items to access it, unlike the true blood altar. Each [[dark essence fragment]] yields 23.8 Runecraft experience, not including the 0.625 Runecraft experience from binding the dense essence. Each [[dark essence block]] yields 95.2 Runecraft experience and an additional 2.5 experience for binding it at the [[dark altar]]. It is possible to reach approximately 38,000 experience per hour crafting blood runes in Arceuus. Using the full [[graceful outfit]] and having 78+ [[Agility]] should be enough to have enough run energy to last the whole trip, depending on how often the [[dense runestone]] depletes. With an [[achievement diary cape]], the [[Abyss]] can be used by teleporting to [[Lesser Fanatic]], to achieve slightly higher experience rates of approximately 45,000 per hour at peak efficiency, although it involves a slight risk of being attacked by other players. Alternatively, the [[Blood Altar|true Blood Altar]] in [[Meiyerditch Laboratories]] requires completion of [[Sins of the Father]], where each [[pure essence]] used yields 10.5 Runecraft [[experience]]. The quest is also required to use the [[Guardian of Blood]] in the [[Guardians of the Rift]] [[minigame]] for crafting blood runes with [[guardian essence]]. If not entering through Guardians of the Rift, a [[blood tiara]], [[blood talisman]], [[catalytic talisman]], [[catalytic tiara]], or [[Runecraft cape]] is required to enter the altar. Using the abyss to craft blood runes in Meiyerditch Laboratories provides approximately double the amount of runes crafted per hour compared to crafting at Arceuus, with only slightly more experience due to the difference in experience per essence, though Arceuus requires less actions and focus, and is less dangerous due to not needing to enter the Wilderness, while also providing a small amount of Mining and Crafting experience. Blood runes can also be crafted at the [[Ourania altar]] below level 77 Runecraft, however they are received relatively rarely. ===True Blood Altar=== {{Tabber |tab1=Pure essence |tab1content={{Recipe |skill1 = Runecraft |skill1lvl = 77 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 10.5 |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} Completed [[Sins of the Father]] |members = Yes |ticks = 1 |facilities = Blood Altar |tools = Blood tiara, Blood talisman |mat1 = Pure essence |output1 = Blood rune }} |tab2=Daeyalt essence |tab2content={{Recipe |skill1 = Runecraft |skill1lvl = 77 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 15.7 |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} Completed [[Sins of the Father]] |members = Yes |ticks = 1 |facilities = Blood Altar |tools = Blood tiara, Blood talisman |mat1 = Daeyalt essence |mat1cost = no |output1 = Blood rune }} |tab3=Guardian essence |tab3content={{Recipe |skill1 = Runecraft |skill1lvl = 77 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 10.5 |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} Completed [[Sins of the Father]]

revision.text:
{{External|rs}} '''Blood spells''' are one of four types of [[Ancient Magicks]] combat spells. Blood spells have a [[life leech]] effect which heals the caster by 25% of the damage dealt; the amount healed is based off of damage the spell would have done, allowing players to heal normally from targets with very little remaining health, or immune to damage from the spell. Clever use of blood spells can trivialize dangerous encounters or compensate for player mistakes during hard content, though they are much more expensive than other types of combat magic. Upon activation of the life leech effect of a blood spell, the message {{Mes|You drain some of your opponent's health.}} will be displayed. A few enemies are immune to the life leech from blood spells; namely, [[Zebak]], the wights in [[Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire]], [[Sotetseg]] and both [[Tumeken's Warden|Tumeken's]] and [[Elidinis' Warden]]. Players can increase the health returned by equipping [[bloodbark armour]]; where each piece increases the amount healed by 2% of the damage dealt, up to a maximum of 35%. All variants of the [[ancient sceptre]] increase the healing effect by 10%, increasing the healing from 25% to 27.5% of damage dealt, or 38.5% with full bloodbark, while the [[blood ancient sceptre]] allows for over-healing Hitpoints up to 10% above the current maximum. The [[Sanguinesti staff]] is a powered staff whose built-in spell is also considered blood magic, though is unaffected by Bloodbark armour. This spell can be used regardless of which spellbook is active. Blood spells may refer to: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" ! rowspan="2" |Icon ! rowspan="2" |[[Mobile]]
icon ! rowspan="2" |Spell ! rowspan="2" |Level ! rowspan="2" | Runes ! rowspan="2" |XP ! rowspan="2" |Cost ! rowspan="2" |Base damage ! colspan="2" |Base Healing {{efn|If hitting for full damage on a single target. Blood burst and Blood barrage may heal from multiple targets.|name=estimate}} |- ! Default !Full bloodbark |- |[[File:Blood Rush.png]] |[[File:Blood Rush icon (mobile).png]] |[[Blood Rush]] |{{SCP|Magic|56}} |{{RuneReq|Blood=1|Death=2|Chaos=2}} |33 |{{Coins|({{GEP|Death rune}} + {{GEP|Chaos rune}} ) * 2 + {{GEP|Blood rune}}}} |15 |3 |4 |- |[[File:Blood Burst.png]] |[[File:Blood Burst icon (mobile).png]] |[[Blood Burst]] |{{SCP|Magic|68}} |{{RuneReq|Death=2|Blood=2|Chaos=4}} |39 | {{Coins|({{GEP|Death rune}} * 2 ) + ({{GEP|Chaos rune}} * 4) + ({{GEP|Blood rune}} * 2)}} |21 |5 |6 |- |[[File:Blood Blitz.png]] |[[File:Blood Blitz icon (mobile).png]] |[[Blood Blitz]] |{{SCP|Magic|80}} |{{RuneReq|Death=2|Blood=4}} |45 |{{Coins|({{GEP|Death rune}} * 2 ) + ({{GEP|Blood rune}} * 4)}} |25 |6 |8 |- |[[File:Blood Barrage.png]] |[[File:Blood Barrage icon (mobile).png]] |[[Blood Barrage]] |{{SCP|Magic|92}} | {{RuneReq|Death=4|Blood=4|Soul=1}} |51 |{{Coins|({{GEP|Death rune}} * 4 ) + ({{GEP|Blood rune}} * 4) + {{GEP|Soul rune}}}} |29 |7 |9 |} {{notelist}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 21 June 2023 |update = More Poll 79 Changes |poll = Old School Content Poll 79: Quality of Life |change = The amount of healing percentage for each piece of [[Bloodbark armour]] used with Blood spells was increased from 1.5% to 2%. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ==Gallery== Blood Rush.gif|Blood Rush Blood Burst.gif|Blood Burst Blood Blitz.gif|Blood Blitz Blood Barrage.gif|Blood Barrage {{clear}} {{Ancient Magicks}} {{Combat spells}}

{{External|rs}} {{Otheruses|def=no|the tithes located around Darkmeyer|Blood Tithe (Darkmeyer)}} [[File:Blood tithe pouch detail.png|right|120px]] '''Blood tithes''' are rendered periodically by the rulers of [[Morytania]], the [[vampyre]]s. Officially, a blood tithe is to be taken from every settlement in Morytania, but the only settlement outside of the [[Sanguinesti region]] that is both known and useful to the vampyres is [[Canifis]], which is inhabited by [[werewolves]], who use meat sacrifices in most cases; however, sometimes, they are forced to sacrifice one of their own. [[Port Phasmatys]] is populated entirely by ghosts, who thus cannot pay the tithe, and nearly every person in [[Mort'ton]] is [[Afflicted]] by the mists from [[Castle Drakan]]; their blood is generally unpleasant, if not poisonous. [[Burgh de Rott]] is not yet known to be populated by those rendering the tithe; although the vampyres have demanded the tithes before, it is not known if the people routinely pay them. Therefore, humans in [[Meiyerditch]] are practically the only ones in Morytania to be forced to pay the blood tithe. In the ghettos, the blood tithe is more than a periodic tax; humans are farmed for blood, each sector being drained at regular intervals. Humans outside the city are comparatively free and well off.
{| class="wikitable" width="85%" ! Settlement !! Has to pay blood tithe !! Notes |- |[[Alice's Farm]]||Yes{{CiteNPC|npc=Lyra|quote=Mother and I must pay a tithe of blood to the vampyres. Father would have protected us, but he is no longer with us, although his presence still walks among us in the fields. We pay with the blood of others.|loc=Garden of Tranquillity}}|| |- |[[Burgh de Rott]]||No||Despite its relative proximity to Sanguinesti region, the vampyres originally believed it was deserted, until [[In Aid of the Myreque]]. However, they were repelled by an adventurer, and have not attempted any action since. |- |[[Canifis]]||Yes||Werewolves pay blood tithe free-willingly, since they are vassals to the vampyres ruling them. |- |[[Darkmeyer]]||Ambiguous||Darkmeyer has a small human population, though they aren't considered citizens, but they are all subjugated as slaves to the vampyres as either [[Prisoner (Darkmeyer)|private]] or [[Blood Tithe (Darkmeyer)|public tithes]]. |- |[[Fenkenstrain's Castle]]||Unclear||During the last stages of his reign, [[Lord Rologarth]] was convinced by [[Dr Fenkenstrain]] to send tribute to the vampyres in the form of unwitting subjects. |- |[[Meiyerditch]]||Yes||This is the main area where blood tithe is taken from humans. It is split into six sectors which are tithed on a rotational basis.{{citeNPC|npc=Garth (Theatre of Blood)|quote=The city is split into sectors so that the vampyres can collect blood tithes on a rotational basis.|loc=A Taste of Hope}} |- |[[Mort'ton]]||No||Mort'ton is currently infected by the so-called Sanguinesti affliction originating from [[Castle Drakan]] which turned humans into [[Afflicted]]. The vampyres originally thought that their blood would be the same as the other humans, but this was proven false after [[Malak]] got sick from consuming their blood. |- |[[Port Phasmatys]]||No||Used to pay blood tithes until the inhabitants of the town were turned into ghosts by [[Necrovarus]], so they no longer have any blood to take. |- |[[Slepe]]||Yes||The villagers pay the blood tithe free-willingly like Canifis, as their founders allied with [[Lowerniel Drakan|Lord Drakan]]. |} The vampyres require blood tithes, as blood is their main dietary staple and energy source, similar to the vampyres of popular culture. It also forces some humans to collaborate with the vampyres to protect their families, such as [[Gadderanks]].
The blood tithes cause fear, suffering and poverty among the Morytanian people, making travelling a danger. Often, it leads to victims being severely weakened, with no energy and will to live, depressed and dying. Sometimes, victims die of blood poisoning or lack of blood, or are taken away and never seen again.
Players travelling in the Sanguinesti region can also be subject to the tithes. At random, [[Vyrewatch]] can ask for one, at which point the player can either choose to be tithed (receive a small amount of damage), be sent to the mines (after [[Darkness of Hallowvale]]), attack the Vyrewatch (although they cannot be harmed, before said quest), or to try and distract the Vyrewatch (success depends on the player's [[Thieving]] level). [[Vyrewatch clothing]] reduces the chance of being seen by the Vyrewatch.

revision.text:
{{Infobox Item |name = Bloody diary |image = [[File:Bloody diary.png]] |release = [[25 July]] [[2019]] |update = Song of the Elves |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = |options = Read, Drop |examine = Most of the pages are stained with blood and have become illegible. |value = 1 |weight = 0.226 |id = 24055 }} [[File:Bloody diary detail.png|left|150px]] The '''bloody diary''' is a book found in the [[Grand Library]] in [[Prifddinas]], which requires completion of [[Song of the Elves]] to access.
The diary was written during the [[Great_Kourend#War_of_the_Five_Houses|War of the Five Houses]] 200 years ago by an unnamed adventurer from [[Hosidius]]. However, most of the pages have been stained in blood and cannot be read by the player.
The few entries that remain unstained describes the adventurer's return to [[Great Kourend]] after the war, some of his adventures in [[Varlamore]], as well as nearly discovering how to create [[Arclight]].
If lost, it can be reclaimed from any bookshelf in the Grand Library, or from a [[bookcase]] within a [[player-owned house]].
==Transcript== {{Hastranscript|Bloody diary|transclude=yes}}
==Gallery== <gallery mode="packed" heights="150" style="text-align:center"> Bloody diary (interface, 1).png|Pages 1-2 Bloody diary (interface, 2).png|Pages 3-4 Bloody diary (interface, 3).png|Pages 5-6 Bloody diary (interface, 4).png|Pages 7-8 Bloody diary (interface, 5).png|Pages 9-10 Bloody diary (interface, 6).png|Pages 11-12 Bloody diary (interface, 7).png|Pages 13-14 Bloody diary (interface, 8).png|Pages 15-16 </gallery>
==Trivia== * The Bloody Diary was written by a player named ''Spineweilder'' in response to Mod Wolf's request for lore book submissions after answering a question during the weekly Q&A stream on 27 March 2019 about the origin of [[Arclight]], as there was no backstory given to the sword compared to its predecessors, [[Silverlight]] and [[Darklight]]. ** The diary was then used as the player's submission for the [[Song of the Elves]] lore writing competition, in which their name can be found in-game by searching the [[Desk (Tower of Voices)|desk]] by the [[Elven Crystal Chest]] in the [[Tower of Voices]]. In addition, they were sent an engraved crystal decoration in real life to commemorate the quest. *The Bloody Diary mentions the Colossal Wyrm, the [[Colossal Wyrm Remains|remains]] of which can be found in the [[Colossal Wyrm Agility Course]]. This content would not be added to the game until [[Update:Varlamore: The Rising Darkness is OUT NOW|2024]], five years after the diary's addition.
{{Grand Library}} [[Category:Texts and tomes]] [[Category:Storable in Bookcase]]

revision.text:
{{Infobox Item |name = Bloody head |image = [[File:Bloody head.png]] |release = [[25 November]] [[2020]] |update = Twisted Tales - Getting Ahead Launch |members = Yes |quest = [[Getting Ahead]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Destroy |destroy = You'll need to sculpt another head out of clay before attaching some fur and dyeing the result red. |examine = A badly sculpted clay head covered in fur and 'blood'. |value = 300 |alchable = No |weight = 0.907 |id = 25147 }} [[File:Bloody head detail.png|left|130px]] The '''bloody head''' is an item created during the quest [[Getting Ahead]] by using [[red dye]] on a [[fur head]]. It is used to finally convince [[Gordon]] that players have killed the [[Headless Beast]] after failing to do so with a fur head prior.
It is mounted in [[Gordon]] and [[Mary (Getting Ahead)|Mary's]] house.
The player can only have one bloody head at a time. Attempting to craft another with a bloody head in the player's inventory results in the chatbox stating "You already have a bloody head." If the player banks the bloody head and crafts another one in the inventory, the bloody head stored in the bank is destroyed. After mounting a bloody head to the [[Mounted Head Space (Getting Ahead)|Mounted Head Space]] in Gordon and Mary's house, the bloody head (and other fake head variants) are destroyed and can no longer be crafted again.
The bloody head is destroyed upon [[death]]. If lost during the quest, the player needs to craft another.
This item cannot leave a placeholder in the bank.
{{Getting Ahead}}

{{Infobox Item |name = Bloody notes |image = [[File:Bloody notes.png]] |release = [[27 January]] [[2021]] |update = Shades of Mort'ton Rework |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Read, Drop |examine = A worn diary with a blood red cover. |value = 2 |weight = 0.003 |id = 25476 |leagueRegion = Morytania }} [[File:Bloody notes detail.png|left|140px]] The '''bloody notes''' is a diary obtained from chests within the [[Shade Catacombs]]. Higher tier chests give a higher chance of obtaining the journal, as well as wearing a [[ring of wealth]]. Opening the notes for the first time gives players a [[runescroll of bloodbark]], which can be read to unlock the ability to create [[bloodbark armour]].
When the notes are first opened, a message in the chatbox will state "''As you open the ancient notes, a rough scroll falls out.''" After having read the book once, the player will from now on receive the accompanying scroll as a reward from the chest whenever otherwise a book would have been obtained.
Written by [[Otrava]] prior to her conversion to [[Zamorak]] during the early years of the [[Third Age]], the journal describes her experiences with a great hollow tree near the ruins of [[Flamtaer]] whom she referred to as the Chatter Tree.
The notes can be retrieved from the bookcase in a [[player-owned house]].
==Transcript== {{Hastranscript|Bloody notes|transclude=Yes}}
==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Bloody notes}}
==Gallery== <gallery mode="packed" heights="150" style="text-align:center"> File:Bloody notes (interface, 1).png|Pages 1-2 File:Bloody notes (interface, 2).png|Pages 3-4 File:Bloody notes (interface, 3).png|Pages 5-6 File:Bloody notes (interface, 4).png|Pages 7-8 </gallery>

{{external|rs}} {{Infobox NPC |version1 = Normal |version2 = Cutscene |name = Blue Opal Director |image = [[File:Blue Opal Director.png|180px]] |release = [[31 May]] [[2005]] |update = Keldagrim - The Dwarven City |members = Yes |race = [[Dwarf]] |quest = [[The Giant Dwarf]] |location = [[Keldagrim]] |gender = Male |options1 = Talk-to |options2 = N/A |examine = One of the leaders of the business Consortium, a ruler of Keldagrim. |map = {{Map|name=Blue Opal Director|2870,10203|mapID=10|plane=1|rectX=8|rectY=6|mtype=rectangle}} |id1 = 5999 |id2 = 2221 |leagueRegion = Fremennik }} [[File:Blue Opal Director chathead.png|left]] The '''Blue Opal Director''' is the leader of the [[Blue Opal]] Mining Company, one of the eight companies that form the [[Consortium]] that governs the [[dwarven]] capital city of [[Keldagrim]].
As a director, it is his job to ensure not only that his company is properly managed, but also that [[Keldagrim]] is governed well, while paying particular attention to the city's booming economy.
During [[The Giant Dwarf]], players may join the Blue Opal company. To do this, they must first do a series of item-retrieval tasks for the [[Blue Opal Secretary]], and then do a series of tasks for the director. If they join the company, the director's head will be featured atop the statue that stands on the [[River Kelda]].
==Dialogue== {{hastranscript|npc}}
{{The Giant Dwarf}} {{Consortium}} {{Keldagrim}} [[Category:Dwarves]][[Category:Monarchs and Rulers]]

{{external|rs}} {{Infobox NPC |name = Blue Opal Secretary |image = [[File:Blue Opal Secretary.png|170px]] |release = [[31 May]] [[2005]] |update = Keldagrim - The Dwarven City |members = Yes |race = [[Dwarf]] |quest = [[The Giant Dwarf]] |location = [[Keldagrim]] |gender = Male |options = Talk-to |examine = The head secretary of the Blue Opal mining company. |map = {{Map|name=Blue Opal Secretary|x=2869|y=10205|mapID=10|plane=1|r=2|mtype=square}} |id = 5992 |leagueRegion = Fremennik }} [[File:Blue Opal Secretary chathead.png|left]] The '''Blue Opal Secretary''' is the head secretary for the [[Blue Opal]] mining company, one of the eight companies that form the [[Consortium]] and rule the [[dwarven]] capital of [[Keldagrim]].
The secretary assists the [[Blue Opal Director]], who manages the company. The secretary ensures that the director is not overburned by paperwork, and also helps to manage smaller affairs such as greeting traders and shooing adventurers out of the company's office.
The secretary also plays a role during [[The Giant Dwarf]]. If the player wishes to join the company, they must first run a series of errands for him, which revolve around retrieving ore in a short amount of time. After the quest is complete, players may also receive [[Keldagrim tasks|tasks]] from him. If completed, they will be rewarded with either [[Mining]] experience or [[coins]].
==Dialogue== {{hastranscript|npc}}
{{The Giant Dwarf}} {{Consortium}} {{Keldagrim}} [[Category:Dwarves]] [[Category:Seated NPCs]]

{{External|rs=Sick-looking sheep (3)|rsc=3rd plague sheep}} {{Infobox NPC |version1 = Sick |version2 = Dyed |name = Blue Sheep |image1 = [[File:Blue Sheep.png|250px]] |image2 = [[File:Blue Sheep (dyed).png|250px]] |release1 = [[15 August]] [[2002]] |release2 = [[19 July]] [[2005]] |update1 = Sheep and cults |update2 = Plague City Series Continued |members = Yes |race = [[Sheep]] |quest1 = [[Sheep Herder]]

Its wool is slightly bluish. Once killed, it drops the [[sheep bones (3)]]. After [[Mourning's End Part I]], the sheep are of a darker blue as a result of the player dyeing them with a [[Fixed device]] loaded with a [[Blue toad]]. Once dyed, they can no longer be prodded or interacted with in any way. Luckily, players only need to dye one and all the sheep of the same colour turn dark. |immunethrall = No |id1 = 14103 |id2 = 14104 }} }} '''Blue dragons''' are the third strongest of the [[chromatic dragons]], behind [[red dragon]]s and [[black dragon]]s. Like all dragons, they can breathe [[dragonfire]], which can inflict up to 50 damage if proper protections aren't used. Dragonfire can be mitigated by equipping an [[anti-dragon shield]] or a [[dragonfire shield]] – alongside the usage of an [[antifire potion]], which will completely negate dragonfire damage. On top of the strong dragonfire breath, they also attack with an accurate slash attack. Blue dragons are assignable as a [[Slayer task]] after starting [[Dragon Slayer I]]. [[Baby blue dragon]]s also count toward blue dragon tasks, and can be found within the [[Myths' Guild]], [[Isle of Souls Dungeon|Isle of Souls]], or the [[Taverley Dungeon]]. A variant of blue dragons are found in the [[Ruins of Tapoyauik]] that are uniquely weak to [[fire spells]], instead of [[water spells|water]] like most chromatic dragons. With a surprisingly fast respawn time of around 20 seconds, even areas with single spawns are suitable for training or collecting resources. Two are fought during [[Dragon Slayer II]]. ==Locations== {{LocTableHead}} {{LocLine |name = Blue dragon |location = [[Corsair Cove Dungeon]]/[[Myths' Guild|Myths' Guild (basement)]]{{Refn|Requires safespot.png|Safespot found in the [[Heroes' Guild]]. Blue dragon (Ogre Enclave) safespot.png|Safespot found within the [[Ogre Enclave]]. Blue dragon (Ogre Enclave) safespot 2.png|A safespot for two dragons found in the Ogre Enclave. Blue dragon (Taverley Dungeon) safespot.png|Safespot found within the [[Taverley Dungeon]]. Can be used with either Ranged, Magic, or Melee. Blue dragon (Isle of Souls Dungeon) safespot.png|Safespot found within the [[Isle of Souls Dungeon]]. Blue dragon (Dragon Nest) safespot.png|Safespot found within the [[Dragon Nest]] east of [[Tal Teklan]]. ==Protections from dragonfire== The following methods will provide partial protection: *'''An [[anti-dragon shield]] or a [[dragonfire shield]] (''permanent''):''' offers high protection, significantly reducing dragonfire damage. *'''An [[antifire potion]] (''temporary''):''' offers partial protection, resulting in damage reduction generally with resistance similar to the shield mentioned above. Occasionally, you may be 'horribly burnt by the dragon fire', receiving moderate damage. The following methods will provide '''100% protection''', but each has its pros and cons: *'''An antifire potion + an anti-dragon or a dragonfire shield:''' temporary but saves a large amount of [[food]] considering how long each potion lasts. This method is strongly recommended as you can use prayer flicking to [[Protect from Melee]], ultimately negating 100% of damage. *'''An antifire potion or anti-dragon/dragonfire shield + [[Protect from Magic]]:''' not advised due to the high cost of [[prayer potion]]s, this is only recommended for players with a high [[Prayer]] level. Alternatively, prayer flicking is an option. This leaves players vulnerable to melee attacks, however. *'''A [[super antifire potion]]:''' More expensive than antifire potions, but they fully protect from dragonfire, allowing the use of a better shield or defender. ==Safespotting== Alternate methods to avoid usage of potions includes the [[Heroes' Guild]], which has a blue dragon in a fenced off area that can be safespotted. If one has partially completed [[Watchtower]], there are [[safespot]]s in the [[Ogre Enclave]] with six dragons that spawn. [[Taverley Dungeon]] also has some safespots with the use of the columns and [[big egg]]s. In the upper level to the north-west there are some rocks you can safespot behind. You can also stand at the top of the stairs and safespot the closest dragon between the eggs and stalagmite. In the passageway to the black demons next to the agility shortcut a single blue dragon and baby blue dragon can be safespotted. Below the [[Myths' Guild]], in the [[Corsair Cove Dungeon]], there are multiple safespots and practically no competition from other players, as the requirements to get there are quite high. There are three [[safespots]] in the [[Isle of Souls Dungeon]]. One is in the cul-de-sac of stalagmites that contain two [[adamantite rocks]] in the eastern part of the room. Simply walk within the stalagmites, east, and you will be out of the reach of [[Blue dragon|blue dragon's]] attack. The second is in the northern passage of the blue dragon room. Position yourself in the northern passage. There is a level 25 [[skeleton]] patrolling the northern passage. The dragons cannot reach you up by the [[skeleton]]. You can attack with [[Range weapons|range]] from here. You can also get a [[baby blue dragon]] caught in between you and the blue dragon, which will act as a barrier. Third is by the south-eastern passage that leads to the [[iron dragon]]s. The player can safely attack from behind the decorative skeleton located near the thievable [[Chest (Isle of Souls Dungeon)|chest]]. Both an adult and a baby blue dragon are within safespotting range. The dragons residing in the [[Ruins of Tapoyauik]] can be safespotted from behind some ice chunks in the northern side of their area of the dungeon. If you intend to [[Magic|mage]] them note that the dragons here are weak to fire as opposed to water like all other blue dragons. Alternative safespot when fighting them in the south-western chamber can be between the southern wall and westernmost pillar, next to some ice chunks. While using the safe spot pictured above in [[Taverley Dungeon]], you can also use a [[halberd]] to safe spot with melee. ==Money making== {{Mmgsection|Killing blue dragons}} ==Drops== {{External|rs}} {{otheruses|the [[Barbarian Assault]] egg|the egg received from [[bird nest]]s|Bird's egg}} {{Infobox Item |name = Blue egg |image = [[File:Blue egg.png]] |release = [[4 January]] [[2007]] |update = Barbarian Assault |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Destroy |examine = Stun your foes! |value = 100 |alchable = No |weight = 0.020 |id = 10533 }}[[File:Blue egg detail.png|left|100px]] '''Blue eggs''' are used in [[Barbarian Assault]] to [[Stun (status)|stun]] penance monsters. If loaded into an [[egg launcher]] and shot at [[penance]] creatures, a blue egg will stun its target for 6 seconds. During this time, the monster will not move, and cannot be targeted with food, weapons or the egg launcher. A maximum of five blue eggs may be loaded into the egg launcher at any given time. Both egg launchers share the same reserve of eggs. Blue eggs are rarely used in the minigame due to the fact that firing one will render its target temporarily unattackable (and, in the case of [[penance healer|healers]], unable to be poisoned). However, they can still be useful for slowing down [[Penance runner]]s from reaching the southern cave entrance should they manage to get past the player(s) who are assigned the Defender role. {{bug|A blue egg that hits a monster with zero hitpoints can cancel its death animation, making it immune to attacks until it has regenerated health.}} ==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Blue egg}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 20 January 2021 |update = Puro-Puro Improvements and Barbarian Assault Changes |change = Barbarian Assault eggs have been remodelled to be more colourblind friendly. }} {{Subject changes |date = 6 January 2021 |update = Soul Wars And 20th Anniversary Event |change = The item's [[value]] was changed from 100,000,000 to 100. }} {{Subject changes |date = 8 March 2018 |update = Tournament Worlds: Theatre of Blood rewards |change = Shift-clicking will now destroy the item. }} {{Subject changes |date = 11 August 2016 |update = Elder Chaos Druid Hood & Junk |change = The item's value was increased from 1 to 100,000,000. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Blue egg (v1) detail.png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Blue egg detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Blue egg v1.png|center]] |[[File:Blue egg.png|center]] |- |4 January 2007 –

{{Otheruses|cooked bluefin|the raw form|raw bluefin}} {{Infobox Item |name = Bluefin |image = [[File:Bluefin.png]] |release = [[19 November]] [[2025]] |update = Sailing is OUT TODAY! |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Eat, Drop |examine = Some nicely cooked bluefin. |value = 170 |weight = 0.650 |exchange = Yes |id = 32344 }} [[File:Bluefin detail.png|130px|left]] '''Bluefin''' is a type of [[fish]] that restores 22 [[Hitpoints]] and 5 [[prayer points]] when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking [[raw bluefin]] on a [[fire]] or [[cooking range]], requiring level 87 [[Cooking]] and granting 215 [[experience]] when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a [[burnt bluefin]]. The [[burn rate]] decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will only stop burning at level 99 when cooking at the [[Hosidius Kitchen]] with the elite [[Kourend & Kebos Diary]] completed, or when wearing a [[Cooking cape]]. ==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Cooking |skill1lvl = 87 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 215 |members = Yes |ticks = 4 |facilities = Cooking range |mat1 = Raw bluefin |output1 = Bluefin }} ===Cooking chance=== {{DropLogProject|jagex=yes|success=yes}} {{Skilling success chart|label=Bluefin cooking chance|showbefore=no |label1=Fire|low1=-1007|high1=222|req1=87|color1=orange|image1=Firemaking icon.png |label2=Range|low2=-997|high2=232|req2=87|color2=saddlebrown|image2=Cooking range icon.png |label3=Hosidius +5%|low3=-985|high3=244|req3=87|color3=red|image3=Cooking range icon.png |label4=Hosidius +10%|low4=-972|high4=257|req4=87|color4=blue|image4=Cooking range icon.png }} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 13 May 2026 |update = Sailing Changes and Gem Bag Expansion |change = The item was graphically updated to be more vibrant. }} {{Subject changes |date = 3 July 2025 |update = Introducing a New Renderer for the Official Client! |change = Removed from the beta cache with the end of the [[June 2025 Sailing Alpha|Sailing Beta]]. }} {{Subject changes |date = 26 June 2025 |update = Sailing Beta - Available Now On Desktop or Mobile |change = Added to the beta cache during the Sailing Beta. It is obtained by talking to the [[Jungle Forester]] in the [[Kharazi Jungle]], south-east of [[Shilo Village (location)|Shilo Village]].
