revision.text:
{{External|rs=Blurberry Special|rsc}} {{Infobox Item |name = Blurberry special |image = [[File:Blurberry special.png]] |release = [[12 December]] [[2002]] |update = Agility skill online |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Drink, Drop |examine = Looks good... smells strong. |value = 30 |weight = 0.500 |exchange = Yes |id = 2064 }} [[File:Blurberry special detail.png|left|120px]] The '''Blurberry special''' can be mixed with 1 [[vodka]], 1 [[brandy]], 1 [[gin]], 1 [[orange]], and 2 [[lemon]]s. It can be finished by adding 1 [[equa leaves|equa leaf]], 1 [[lime slices|sliced lime]], 1 [[lemon chunks|diced lemon]], and 1 [[orange chunks|diced orange]] as a garnish. This requires 37 [[Cooking]] to make. All of these ingredients can be purchased at [[Funch's Fine Groceries]] and cost a total of 30 coins per Blurberry special made (not including [[cocktail shaker]], [[cocktail glass]], or [[knife]]). A [[Premade blurb' sp.]] (premade Blurberry special) can be purchased at the [[Blurberry Bar]] for 30 coins. It heals 7 [[Hitpoints]], increases [[Strength]] by 5% + 2 levels, and reduces [[Attack]] by 2% - 3 levels. A Blurberry special (fresh or premade) may be given to [[Harold]] during the [[Death Plateau]] quest to make the gambling section of the quest far easier, as it will cause him to become so drunk he assumes you win every dice game you play with him. ==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Cooking |skill1lvl = 37 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 150 |members = Yes |ticks = 1 |mat1 = Mixed special |mat1cost = No |mat2 = Lemon chunks |mat3 = Orange chunks |mat4 = Equa leaves |mat5 = Lime slices |output1 = Blurberry special |mat6=Cocktail glass}} ==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Blurberry special}} ===Shop locations=== {{Store locations list|Blurberry special}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 7 August 2006 |update = Gnome Cuisine |change = The item was graphically updated with the rework of the [[Gnome Restaurant]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Blurberry special detail (beta).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Blurberry special detail (historical).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Blurberry special detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Blurberry special (beta).png|center]] |[[File:Blurberry special (historical).png|center]] |[[File:Blurberry special.png|center]] |- |RuneScape 2

revision.text:
{{Otheruses|boats used in the Sailing skill|non-Sailing boats|Ship}} A '''boat''' (sometimes referred to as a '''ship''' or '''player-owned ship''') is a vessel used to train the [[Sailing]] skill. They can be used to travel between [[mooring point]]s and to engage with various activities at sea, including [[salvaging]], [[Barracuda trials]], [[sea charting]], and [[port tasks]]. Boats can be purchased from any [[shipwright]] after completion of the [[Pandemonium]] quest. To board a boat, use the [[Gangplank (Sailing)|gangplank]] or [[Mooring point (scenery)|mooring point]] at the port or island where the boat is located. A boat's location can be set by disembarking, by clicking a [[Buoy (Sailing)|buoy]] at sea, or by speaking to a [[shipwright]], who can call a [[port wizard]] to summon it. Boats can only be located at a single port at a time. At level 1 Sailing, players may own only one boat, but more boats can be owned at higher levels: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !Level !Boats |- |1 || 1 |- |15 || 2 |- |50 || 3 |- |78 || 4 |- |91 || 5 |} ==Types of boats== Different types of boats have different Sailing level requirements to obtain and use. All boats have a base number of hitpoints, which can be improved through [[Shipbuilding|upgrading]] the [[hull]]. A raft can be obtained as a reward for completing the [[Pandemonium]] quest. The required levels are not boostable. {| class="wikitable sortable align-center-1 align-center-4 align-center-7 align-center-8 align-center-9" ! {{SCP|Sailing}} Level !colspan="2" class="unsortable"| [[Boat]] !class="unsortable"| Image ! [[Game square|Size]] ! Core boat parts ! [[Facility hotspot]]s ! Player capacity ! [[Crew Management|Crew slots]] ! Cost |- |1 |{{plinkt|Raft|pic=Raft icon}} |[[File:Raft.png|125x120px]] |Tiny
(1x3) | *[[Hull]] *[[Helm]] *[[Mast and sails]] |1 |2 |0 |{{Coins|1000}} |- |15 |{{plinkt|Skiff|pic=Skiff icon}} |[[File:Skiff.png|125x120px]] |Small
(2x5) | *[[Hull]] *[[Helm]] *[[Mast and sails]] *[[Keel]] |7 |5 |2 |{{Coins|15000}} |- |50 |{{plinkt|Sloop|pic=Sloop icon}} |[[File:Sloop.png|125x120px]] |Medium
(3x10) | *[[Hull]] *[[Helm]] *[[Mast and sails]] *[[Keel]] |11 |10 |5 |{{Coins|200000}} |} Broadly speaking: * A raft is tiny, simple to upgrade and very cheap to [[Shipwright|teleport around]] for quick access to sailing in any port. But it is quite fragile and has only a single hotspot for either the cargo hold, or other [[facilities]]. * A skiff is fast and mobile, with enough space and several facilities more than sufficient for exploring. * A sloop is large and sturdy, with numerous hotspots for multiple seafaring activities and well-equipped for combat. It is, however, hugely expensive to upgrade or retrieve, and cannot fit in certain small spaces. It's a good idea to own all three boat types when available, since the skiff is required for [[Barracuda Trials]], only the raft can access certain locations for [[sea charting]], and the sloop is a noticeable upgrade in terms of storage space and efficiency of [[Ship combat|combat]], [[shipwreck salvaging|salvaging]] and [[deep sea trawling|sea trawling]]. == Damage and repair == Like players, boats have hitpoints based on their [[hull]] and [[keel]]; however, unlike players, boat hitpoints do not recover over time. Damage to a boat can be recovered in multiple ways: * When a hull or keel is upgraded, a boat will be restored to its maximum health. * [[Shipwright Seb]] in the [[shipyard]] can repair a boat for {{NoCoins|50}} coins per missing hitpoints. This fee can be taken directly from the bank. * Players may use [[repair kits]] on the boat to restore different amounts of hitpoints based on the level of the kit. If a boat's hitpoints drop to 0, the boat will [[Sailing#Death & Capsizing|capsize]]. Capsized boats can be retrieved by speaking to any [[shipwright]], who will call a [[port wizard]] to retrieve the boat for a fee. If a boat capsizes, a player teleports from their boat while at sea, or a player dies on their boat while at sea, all courier crates, bounty items, shipwreck salvage, trawling fish, and fish-filled crates will be lost from the [[cargo hold]]. Other items such as cannonballs, repair kits, fish offcuts, and empty fish crates will be kept. ==Teleportation== [[Summon Boat]] is a spell on the [[standard spellbook]] that requires 56 [[Magic]] and allows a player to instantly move their boat to the nearest [[mooring point]]. Boats must have a [[Teleport focus (facility)|teleport focus]] or [[Greater teleport focus (facility)|greater teleport focus]] installed to be eligible for teleportation. Casting Summon Boat will cause a player to lose all courier crates, bounty items, shipwreck salvage, trawling fish, and fish-filled crates that are stored in the cargo hold. Other items such as cannonballs, repair kits, fish offcuts, and empty fish crates will be kept. [[Teleport to boat]] requires 67 Magic and teleports the player to their boat's location. Boats must have a greater teleport focus to be eligible as a teleport destination. [[Boat bottle]]s are used to store boats and move them to another port. Similarly, players can pay a [[shipwright]] to relocate or recover a capsized boat, though one is not found at every mooring point. Certain drinks in [[sealed crate]]s also can move the boat to specific ports, for example the [[bottle of fishier bladderier stout]] moves it to [[Rellekka]] and the [[bottle of portal nexus perry]] to [[Port Sarim]]. {| class="wikitable" |+Boat Recovery Costs !Type !Base Recovery Cost{{Efn|Recovery fees increase with the amount of damage inflicted on the boat and the components/facilities built on the boat}} |- |[[Raft]] |{{Coins|250}} |- |[[Skiff]] |{{Coins|4125}} |- |[[Sloop]] |{{Coins|50000}} |} {{Notelist}} Most means of teleporting a boat, including capsizing, remove certain items from the [[cargo hold]]: these include salvage, port task crates, bounty task items, and non-empty crates of fish. However, having [[membership]] lapse while at sea then logging in on a [[free-to-play]] world will safely transport a boat to its most recent docking point with all cargo intact. ==Customisation and upgrades== {{Main|Shipbuilding}} [[Shipbuilding]] allows for customisation and upgrading of a boat through the addition of [[facilities]] and improved ship components such as [[hull]]s, [[helm]]s, and [[keel]]s. Different types of boats allow for different numbers of facilities and different levels of component customisation. The [[Shipyard]] is used to customise boats. It can be accessed by speaking to any [[shipwright]]. {| class="wikitable" !Type !Facilities !Facility types |- |[[Raft]] |1 | [[Cargo hold]], [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannon]], [[salvaging hook]], [[wind catcher]] |- |[[Skiff]] |7 | [[Cargo hold]], [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannon]], [[salvaging hook]], [[wind catcher]], [[Anchor (Sailing)|anchor]], [[Innoculation station|inoculation station]] |- |[[Sloop]] |9 |[[Cargo hold]], [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannon]], [[salvaging hook]], [[wind catcher]], [[Anchor (Sailing)|anchor]], [[Innoculation station|inoculation station]] |} ==Guest access and world switching== Other players, including [[Ironman Mode|ironmen]], may enter a host's vessel by selecting the Board-friend option on a gangplank or mooring point. However, if you [[World switching|switch worlds]] while on another person's boat, you will end up on [[Limbo]] until you hop back to the world they are on. If switching worlds while on your own boat, your boat will switch with you and you will remain in the same location. Additionally, your crewmates will briefly stop working until they move back into their assigned positions. ==Destroy a boat== Players can destroy their boat by speaking with any [[shipwright]]. This can be beneficial if wishing to replace one boat with another, for example to replace a raft with a different type of boat. It can also be used to re-roll the randomly generated name given to a boat prior to having access to [[Sleve McDichael]] at 61 [[Sailing]], although this alternative can be expensive for [[sloop]]s. ==Boat names== {{main|Boat name}} Boats are randomly assigned a name when purchased, but this name can be changed at [[Sleve McDichael]] on the [[Tear of the Soul]], who will randomly select a new name for any boat for the cost of one unnoted [[cider]]. At level 99, players can use the [[Sailing cape|Sailing skillcape]] perk to rename their boat at any time with the descriptor and noun individually chosen from a list. ==Transcript== {{hastranscript}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 3 December 2025 |update = Sailing XP Review & Further Fixes |change = Boats will now heal to full whenever their keel or hull is upgraded. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ==Trivia== * Attempting to light a fire on your boat will display the message {{mes|The boat is too damp and unstable to light a fire here.}} * Attempting to place a [[dwarf multicannon]] on your boat will display the message {{mes|The boat is too damp and unstable for you to set up a cannon here.}} {{Shipbuilding}} {{Sailing}}

{{otheruses|other types of Bottles|Bottle|def=no}}{{Infobox Item |version1 = Empty |version2 = Full |name1 = Boat bottle (empty) |name2 = Boat bottle (full) |image1 = [[File:Boat bottle (empty).png]] |image2 = [[File:Boat bottle (full).png]] |release = [[19 November]] [[2025]] |update = Sailing is OUT TODAY! |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable1 = Yes |tradeable2 = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable1 = Yes |noteable2 = No |options1 = Bottle-boat, Drop |options2 = Unbottle-boat, Check, Destroy |examine1 = One has been poured out for (sailing with) the boys. |examine2 = I'm a boat within a bottle, baby, you gotta rub me the right way. |value = 500 |alchable1 = Yes |alchable2 = No |weight = 0.020 |exchange1 = Yes |exchange2 = No |id1 = 31989 |id2 = 31992 |leagueRegion = No }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Boat bottle (empty) detail.png|140px|left]] |version2 = [[File:Boat bottle (full) detail.png|140px|left]] }} '''Boat bottles''' are a single-use item obtained rarely from sorting low-tier [[salvage]] from [[Shipwreck salvaging|shipwrecks]]. It is used to "place" a player's [[boat]] into their inventory, allowing them to transport it to another port from land. This is useful for moving boats without a [[Teleport focus (facility)|teleport focus]] built on them.
Using the "Bottle-boat" option on an empty bottle requires an empty cargo hold, as well as being at a [[File:Docking_point_icon.png|link=]] [[docking point]]. When using the "Unbottle-boat" option on a full bottle, players will receive a confirmation message before doing so. The bottle will be lost when the player releases the boat.
Compared with the cost of recovering a boat in order to move it to a different port, using a boat bottle on a [[raft]] will result in a profit/loss of {{NoCoins|250-{{GEP|Boat bottle (empty)}}|c}}, with a [[skiff]] {{NoCoins|4125-{{GEP|Boat bottle (empty)}}|c}}, and with a [[sloop]] {{NoCoins|50000-{{GEP|Boat bottle (empty)}}|c}}.
If a bottle containing a boat is destroyed, the boat is not lost, and can be recovered at a [[shipwright]].
==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Boat bottle (empty)}}
==Dialogue== {{Hastranscript|item}}
==Trivia== * The empty bottle's examine text is a reference to the saying "[[wiktionary:pour one out|pour one out]]". * The full bottle's examine text is a reference to the song "{{WP|Genie in a Bottle}}" by {{WP|Christina Aguilera}}.
{{Shipbuilding}} [[Category:Collection log items]]

'''Boat paint''' is used to recolour the trim of your [[boat]] using the [[boat schematics]] board at the [[Shipyard]].
The [[skiff]] requires 1 paint, whereas the [[sloop]] requires 2. The [[raft]] cannot be painted. Each trim requires 25 [[Sailing]] and 20 [[Construction]].
Applying a paint to a skiff rewards 10 Construction experience, while painting a sloop rewards 20 Construction experience.
Boat paints can be found in the [[Collection_log#Boat_Paints|Boat Paints collection log]] category.

Bob is shown to be working with another guard named [[Billy, a guard of Falador|Billy]], protecting Falador's northern entrance. Both are assumed to be killed offscreen by [[PKMaster0036]], a [[player spoof]]. Bob and his colleague's deaths allow the player to sneak a statue of [[Saradomin]] out of central Falador unnoticed, eventually allowing them to reach the [[Varrock Palace]] gardens. Billy and Bob cannot be encountered outside the [[cutscene]]. They are also referenced briefly during the [[Ratcatchers]] quest, in which guards in the [[East Ardougne]] mansion occasionally say, "I miss Billy and Bob." ==Dialogue== {{Hastranscript|speaksin}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 10 April 2006 |update = Rag and Bone Man |change = The NPC's chainbody was graphically updated. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Bob, another guard of Falador (historical).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Bob, another guard of Falador.png|center|300x150px]] |- |30 August 2005 –

{{External|rs}} {{confuse|Evil Bob}} {{Infobox NPC |name = Bob |image = [[File:Bob the Jagex cat.png|190px]] |release = [[9 August]] [[2004]] |update = Death Plateau Quest |members = Yes |race = [[Cat]] |quest = [[A Tail of Two Cats]], [[Dragon Slayer II]] |location = [[Asgarnia]], spawns at [[Burthorpe]] |gender = Male |examine = The Jagex cat.
'''During Dragon Slayer II:''' Formerly Robert the Strong, now a cat. |map = {{Map|name=Bob|x=2924|y=3565|r=4|mtype=square}} |id = 2635,2636,4231,8034,8055,8111,8112,8113,8114,8115,8159 |leagueRegion = Asgarnia }} [[File:Bob (cat) chathead.png|left]] '''Bob the Jagex cat''' is an enigmatic black [[cat]] who travels the world of [[Gielinor]] with his girlfriend, [[Neite]], although he generally returns to his human [[Unferth]]'s house every week. Like all cats, his speech can only be understood through the use of the [[catspeak amulet]]. As Bob likes to wander the world, he has one of the largest wander radius of all [[NPC]]s in the game, spawning outside his human Unferth's house in [[Burthorpe]] every time there is a system update, after which he is allowed to roam up to 30,000 tiles in any direction.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/640917755697463296|date=7 September 2015|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/98213|archivedate=13 March 2023|quote=Outside Turael's house. He can go 30k steps in any direction.}} As Bob is essentially able to wander anywhere that is not restricted by physical boundaries, players can run into him at places as far away as [[Edgeville]], [[Port Sarim]], the [[Wise Old Man]]'s house, or even [[Lumbridge]]'s church. It is possible to locate Bob by using the catspeak amulet after it is enchanted in [[A Tail of Two Cats]] which, when operated, will open a menu that looks like a cat's face. By clicking on the whiskers, the dial will rotate. When the eyes light up and a cat meowing sound is heard, Bob can be found in the direction that the dial is pointing. Bob can be venerated in the [[Chapel]] of a [[player-owned house]] if a [[Bob icon]] is built with 71 [[Construction]]. ==History== Bob's earliest memories were of being a kitten, and being raised by [[Gertrude]]. Eventually, he came into the care of [[Unferth]], though Bob often wandered around the world for days, worrying his owner endlessly. During [[A Tail of Two Cats]], Unferth asks an adventurer to help him find Bob, as he had not come back for longer than expected, worrying him greatly. The adventurer, with their cat and [[Hild]], were able to locate Bob. When found, Bob tells the adventurer that he is trying to get the attention of another cat named [[Neite]], who is uninterested in him because she does not know about his past. Bob is later convinced that he is [[Robert the Strong]], but he is unsure because he has no memories. The adventurer and their cat head to [[Sophanem]] to get the [[Sphinx]]'s help, who reveals that Bob is actually Robert the Strong, and his memories as a human have been locked away. Neite, who the Sphinx also teleported to Sophanem, falls in love with Bob and the two go on a journey across Gielinor. Bob gives the adventurer some chores for Unferth to do. Later on in [[Dragon Slayer II]], the adventurer finds Bob to see if he can recall his memories as Robert the Strong during his expedition to [[Lithkren]] in the Fourth Age. Bob doesn't remember anything, and the Sphinx is unable to help. However, the adventurer soon remembers the [[Oneiromancer]], who gives them the [[dream vial]]. The adventurer makes the potion again, and they enter Bob's [[Dream World]]. After beating a dream guardian of his human form, Bob then remembers everything as Robert the Strong and helps the player in finding the [[dragon key piece]]s that were hidden all over the world. Bob told the adventurer that he had personally hidden two of the key pieces; one in an [[Ungael|abandoned Dragonkin fortress]] north of [[Rellekka]], and another on the [[Kharazi Jungle|southern shores of Karamja]]. He also entrusted two of the key pieces to his fellow heroes [[Camorra]] and [[Tristan]]. Camorra went to the far west, while Bob assumed that Tristan's family was still in [[Varrock]]. He warned them that he did not feel comfortable with opening the Vault, and that they should do so at their own risk. After the player reforges the key, they enter the Vault and find a [[Galvek|dragon]] incubating in a large pool. [[Zorgoth]], a Dragonkin, approached the trio, and Bob immediately recognised him. Zorgoth also recognised Bob as a result, and remarked on how he turned into a cat. The two argued over who was right and wrong, before Zorgoth called for Galvek. Bob narrowly avoided being incinerated by Galvek, as the adventurer grabbed him and ran. He later attended a meeting with the human leaders, and told the adventurer that the war wouldn't be over until Zorgoth was dealt with. He noted that if Galvek was killed, Zorgoth would lose his army, as Galvek was his only way of controlling the other dragons. While incapable of fighting, Bob insisted on coming along with the assault force, due to his knowledge about the dragonkin. When the adventurer eventually arrived at the fleet's grand ship, Bob informed them of the situation. After disposing of the dragons on the ship, Zorgoth and Galvek arrived. Galvek killed four Varrockian guards, before focusing its attention on the adventurer and launching dragonfire at them. Bob, who was right next to the adventurer, jumps in front of them, sacrificing himself to save their life. Bob's death greatly enraged the adventurer, and they eventually managed to kill Galvek, who accidentally incinerated Zorgoth with his last breath. What was left of Bob was later buried in a [[grave (Bob)|grave]] across from Unferth's house. Both Unferth and Neite were distraught over his death. Upon arriving at the afterlife, Bob met and got along with [[Hogst]]. Hogst told the adventurer to Bob that he missed them and that they shouldn't have guilt for his death, stating that it was necessary. When the adventurer asks why, Hogst states that he does not know. ==Dialogue== {{Hastranscript|npc}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 2 May 2006 |update = Return of the Wise Old Man! |change = Bob's appearance during the cutscene in A Tail of Two Cats was altered. }} {{Subject changes |date = 26 September 2005 |update = A Tail of Two Cats |change = The NPC now always appears above players standing in the same tile. }} {{Subject changes |date = 26 April 2005 |update = Desert Month Finale |change = A 'Talk-to' option was added. }} {{Subject changes |date = 24 August 2004 |update = Troll Stronghold Quest |change = The NPC was renamed from 'Cat' to 'Bob'. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Bob the Jagex cat.png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Bob (cutscene).png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Bob (cat) chathead.png|center]] |[[File:Bob (cutscene) chathead.png|center]] |- |26 September 2005 –
2 May 2006 |2 May 2006 –
present |} ==Trivia== *On release, Bob only had the name 'Cat'. He was renamed to Bob shortly afterwards in response to player suggestions. *The dialogue between Bob and the player's cat follower is clearly a reference to the movie ''{{wp|Star Wars: Episode V – The Empire Strikes Back}}'', where similar dialogue occurs near the end of the movie. *'Bob' is often a nickname given to those bearing the name Robert, which fits due to Bob's past as Robert the Strong. *Originally Bob's death was caused by a Galvek fireball that the player dodges. In 2023, this was changed to Bob jumping in front of the dragonfire aimed at the player. **Bob takes 24 damage from the fireball, which suggests that his [[Hitpoints]] level is 24. *Bob is referenced by [[Hogst]], his friend in the afterlife, in the [[2020 Halloween event]] if the player has completed [[Dragon Slayer II]] and wears a [[ghostspeak amulet]]. The player expresses guilt and misses Bob, but Hogst tells the player not to feel bad about it and recounts a conversation he had with Bob, who cryptically told Hogst his death was 'necessary' and 'had to be that way'. *Bob is referenced by the [[Gnome Child (Realm of Memories)|Gnome Child]] in the [[20th Anniversary event|20th Anniversary Event]]. If Dragon Slayer II is completed, when speaking with the [[Bob|store owner]] of [[Bob's Brilliant Axes]] in Lumbridge, the Gnome Child will insist that they believe that 'Bob is Bob', while the player has the option to insist that Bob is dead and is not coming back. *If [[Dragon Slayer II]] has not been completed when purchasing the [[Max cape]] for the first time, Bob will contact you; if you are wearing a [[Catspeak amulet]] you will understand what he is saying: "Oh most excellently done old chap!" *Bob has some unique dialogue when talking to him in specific locations across the world. In [[Port Sarim]], talking to Bob will cause him to say that he "comes from round here originally" and that "back then all this was just fields". It's unclear if he's referring to where he was born as a cat, or where he was born as [[Robert the Strong]], or if he's not telling the truth in the first place. **If he is referring to where he was born as Robert the Strong, that would suggest [[Arkney]] was located somewhere around where Port Sarim is today. *Bob has several bits of exclusive dialogue when talked to in the [[Wilderness]], but due to the existence of the [[Wilderness Ditch]], it is not possible for Bob to enter the Wilderness and the dialogue is therefore inaccessible. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{A Tail of Two Cats}} {{Dragon Slayer II}} {{NPC Contact}} [[Category:Quest NPCs]] [[Category:Deceased characters]]

{{External|rs=Large essence}} {{Gone}} {{Infobox Item |name = Bob |image = [[File:Bob (unobtainable item).png]] |release = [[20 April]] [[2006]] |update = Rune Essence adjustment |removal = [[7 January]] [[2016]] |removalupdate = Zeah: Great Kourend |members = No |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine = Bobbity bob! |value = 1 |weight = |id = hist7938 }} [[File:Bob (unobtainable item) detail.png|left|120px]] "'''Bob'''" was the name of an unobtainable item that could previously be found in the cache. It was released alongside [[pure essence]], and was supposed to be an item used in more advanced Runecrafting named "Large essence". For unknown reasons, the large essence was not initially added to the game. It was graphically updated in 2006 with the release of [[Lunar Diplomacy]], suggesting it may have been planned to be used when Runecrafting [[astral rune]]s. The item was removed in 2016 and replaced by [[dark essence fragments]], which are used to craft [[Blood rune|blood]] and [[Soul rune|soul]] runes. ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 26 February 2015 |update = The Grand Exchange |change = *The item was renamed from "Bob" to "Null". *The item's examine was changed from "Bobbity bob!" to "null". }} {{Subject changes |date = 24 July 2006 |update = Lunar Diplomacy |change = *The item was graphically updated. *The item's value was increased from 1 to 4. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Bob (unobtainable item) detail (historical).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Bob (unobtainable item) detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Bob (unobtainable item) (historical).png|center]] |[[File:Bob (unobtainable item).png|center]] |- |20 April 2006 ⁠–

{{External|rs=Body altar}} {{Infobox Scenery |name = Altar |image = [[File:Altar (body).png|300px]] |release = [[29 March]] [[2004]] |update = RS2 Launched! |members = No |quest = No |location = South of [[Edgeville Monastery]] |options = Craft-rune |examine = A mysterious power emanates from this shrine. |map = {{Map|mtype=pin|x = 2522|y = 4839|mapID=-1}} |id = 34765 |leagueRegion = Asgarnia }} The '''Body Altar''' is a [[runic altar]] upon which [[body rune]]s are crafted from [[rune essence]] or [[pure essence]], providing 7.5 [[Runecraft]] [[experience]] per essence imbued. Players can also use a [[body core]] to craft body runes, which provides 75 Runecraft experience per core. Level 20 [[Runecraft]] is required to craft body runes.
Players may create a [[body tiara]] here by using either a [[body talisman]] or a [[tiara]] on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 37.5 [[Runecraft]] [[experience]]. A [[catalytic tiara]] can also be created here by using a [[catalytic talisman]] and [[gold tiara]], granting 60 Runecraft experience.
Upon entering the Body Altar, the [[music]] track [[Heart and Mind]] plays.
==Transportation== {{Map|name=Body Altar|align=left|mtype=pin|x = 3052|y = 3444|height = 275|width = 275|caption = The location of the mysterious ruins used to enter the Body Altar.}} The entrance to the altar can be found south of the [[Edgeville Monastery]], between [[Ice Mountain]] and [[Barbarian Village]], the altar can also be accessed through the [[Abyss]].
To enter the [[Mysterious ruins#Body|mysterious ruins]], players either have to use a [[body talisman]] on the ruins, or click "Enter" on the ruins while wearing a [[body tiara]]. Alternatively, a [[catalytic talisman]] or [[catalytic tiara|tiara]] can be used.
The nearest bank is in [[Edgeville]].
==Experience== The maximal amount of body runes that can be crafted in one run is 846, by carrying one [[Giant pouch]] full of essence and 27 [[body core]]s with a Runecraft level of at least 92 (at level 92 players get triple the amount of body runes per essence). This would give 2115 experience.
However, obtaining considerable amounts of body cores is time-consuming.
The maximal amount of body runes crafted in one run without using cores is 162. This would be achieved by having 92 Runecraft and carrying 54 essence to craft (24 in the normal inventory along with 30 in the 4 sizes of [[essence pouch]]es). This would result in 405 experience.
Slightly more experience can be obtained by crafting [[body tiara]]s. A full inventory with 14 [[tiara]]s and 14 [[body talisman]]s would give 525 experience. This is more click-intensive and expensive.
==Products== {{Uses facility list|Body Altar, Catalytic runic altar}}
==Changes==
{{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 23 March 2022 |update = Guardians of the Rift Launch |poll = Old School Content Poll 76: Game Improvements |change = The pre-existing delay after using Essence on Runecraft Altars has been removed. }} {{Subject changes footer}}
==Gallery== <gallery mode="packed" heights="160"> Body Altar outside.png|The entrance to the Body Altar. Body Altar inside.png|The inside of the Body Altar. </gallery>
==Trivia== * When you enter the Body Altar, you spawn on the north of the altar away from the portal unlike the other altars. Curiously, the portal is found in the southern area. * The shape of the temple on the map looks vaguely like a heart and floor colour is pink which matches the heart's colour. * During the music piece, "[[Heart and Mind]]" (which is unlocked by entering the Body Altar), players can hear a beat that sounds like the beating of the heart.

--[[ {{Helper module |name=Paramtest |fname1 = is_empty(arg) |ftype1 = String |fuse1 = Returns true if arg is not defined or contains only whitespace |fname2 = has_content(arg) |ftype2 = String |fuse2 = Returns true if arg exists and does not only contain whitespace |fname3 = default_to(arg1,arg2) |ftype3 = String, Any value |fuse3 = If arg1 exists and does not only contain whitespace, the function returns arg1, otherwise returns arg2 |fname4 = defaults{ {arg1,arg2},...} |ftype4 = {String, Any value}... |fuse4 = Does the same as default_to() run over every table passed; for technical reasons, all nil are replaced with false }} --]] -- -- Tests basic properties of parameters -- local p = {} -- -- Tests if the parameter is empty, all white space, or undefined -- function p.is_empty(arg) return not string.find(arg or '', '%S') end -- -- Returns the parameter if it has any content, the default (2nd param) -- function p.default_to(arg, default) if string.find(arg or '', '%S') then return arg else return default end end -- -- Returns a list of paramaters if it has any content, or the default -- function p.defaults(...) local ret = {} for i, v in ipairs(...) do if string.find(v[1] or '', '%S') then table.insert(ret,v[1]) else -- or false, because nil is removed table.insert(ret,v[2] or false) end end return unpack(ret) end -- -- Tests if the parameter has content -- The same as !is_empty, but this is more readily clear -- function p.has_content(arg) return string.find(arg or '', '%S') end -- -- uppercases first letter -- function p.ucfirst(arg) if not arg or arg:len() == 0 then return nil elseif arg:len() == 1 then return arg:upper() else return arg:sub(1,1):upper() .. arg:sub(2) end end -- -- uppercases first letter, lowercases everything else -- function p.ucflc(arg) if not arg or arg:len() == 0 then return nil elseif arg:len() == 1 then return arg:upper() else return arg:sub(1,1):upper() .. arg:sub(2):lower() end end return p

--[[ {{Helper module|name=Yesno |fname1=(arg) |ftype1=Any value |fuse1=Reads arg for yes/no and returns the appropriate boolean or nil |fname2=(arg1,arg2) |ftype2=Any value, Any value |fuse2=Reads arg1 for yes/no and returns the appropriate boolean; returns arg2 if arg1 was not an applicable value }} --]] -- <pre> -- Used to evaluate args to booleans where applicable -- -- Based on <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Module:Yesno> -- see page history there for contributors --
return function( arg, default ) arg = type( arg ) == 'string' and arg:lower() or arg
if arg == nil then return nil end
if arg == true or arg == 'yes' or arg == 'y' or arg == 'true' or tonumber( arg ) == 1 then return true end
if arg == false or arg == 'no' or arg == 'n' or arg == 'false' or tonumber( arg ) == 0 then return false end
return default end

-- <nowiki> -- -- Implements {{Navbox}} -- require('strict') local p = {} local tnavbar = require( 'Module:Tnavbar' ) local yesno = require( 'Module:Yesno' ) local page_title = mw.title.getCurrentTitle().fullText -- -- Helper for inserting a new row into the navbox -- -- @param tbl {mw.html table} -- @return tbl {mw.html table} -- local function insertRow( tbl ) return tbl:tag( 'tr' ) end
-- -- Creates the navbox table -- -- @param args {table} -- @return tbl {mw.html table} -- local function createTbl( args )
local tbl = mw.html.create( 'table' )
tbl :addClass( yesno(args.subgroup, false) and 'navbox-subgroup' or 'navbox' ) :addClass( 'hlist nowraplinks <mw:editsection' )
if not yesno(args.subgroup, false) and ( args.state == 'collapsed' or args.state == 'uncollapsed' or args.state == 'autocollapse' or -- defaults to autocollapse args.state == nil ) then tbl:addClass( 'mw-collapsible' )
if args.state == 'collapsed' then tbl:addClass( 'mw-collapsed' ) elseif args.state == 'uncollapsed' then tbl:addClass('navbox-uncollapsed') else tbl:addClass( 'mw-collapsed' ) tbl:addClass( 'navbox-autocollapse' ) end end
if yesno(args.collapsible, false) then tbl:addClass( 'navbox-collapsible' ) end
if args.style then tbl:cssText( args.style ) end
-- used by [[MediaWiki:Gadget-navbox-tracking.js]] for tracking purposes tbl:attr( { ['data-navbox-name'] = args.name } )
return tbl end
-- -- Wrapper for [[Module:Tnavbar]] -- -- @param args {table} -- @return {mw.html table} -- local function navbar( args )
local div = mw.html.create( 'div' ) :css( { float = 'left', ['text-align'] = 'left' } ) :wikitext( tnavbar._navbar( { [1] = args.name, ['mini'] = true, ['talk'] = 'autoconfirmed' } ) ) return div end
-- -- Creates the header (what you see when the navbox is collapsed) -- -- @param tbl {mw.html table} -- @param args {table} -- @return {mw.html table} -- local function header( tbl, args ) local div = insertRow( tbl ) :tag( 'th' ) :attr( 'colspan', '2' ) :addClass( 'navbox-title' ) :wikitext( args.name and tostring( navbar( args ) ) ) :tag('div') :addClass( 'navbox-title-name' ) :wikitext( args.title )
return div:allDone() end
-- -- Inserts a row into the navbox -- -- @param tbl {mw.html table} -- @param gtitle {string} -- @param group {string} -- @param gtype {string} -- @param style {string} -- @return {mw.html table} -- local function row( tbl, gtitle, group, gtype, style, _name, subgroup ) local tr = insertRow( tbl ) local td
if gtitle then td = tr :addClass( 'navbox-group' ) :tag( 'th' ) :addClass( 'navbox-group-title' ) :wikitext( gtitle ) :done() :tag( 'td' ) else td = tr :addClass( 'navbox-group' ) :addClass( 'navbox-group-split' ) :tag( 'td' ) :addClass( 'navbox-group-title-hidden' ) :attr( 'colspan', '0' ) :css( 'display', 'none' ) :done() :tag( 'td' ) :attr( 'colspan', '2' ) end
--[[ List styling As an example, it lets you do the following instead if using {{*}} all the time | group3 = * {{plink|foo}} * {{plink|bar}} * {{plink|baz}} ]] if mw.ustring.match( group, '^%s*%*' ) then td:newline()
-- trim whitespace on bullets local spl = mw.text.split( group, '\n' )
for i = 1, #spl do spl[i] = mw.text.trim( spl[i] ) end
group = '\n' .. table.concat( spl, '\n' ) end
td :addClass( 'navbox-list' ) :wikitext( group ) --group3
if gtype and mw.ustring.lower( gtype ) == 'subgroup' then td :addClass( 'navbox-parent' ) :css( { padding = '0' } ) end
if style then td:cssText( style ) end
return td:allDone() end
-- -- Inserts a footer into the navbox -- -- @param tbl {mw.html table} -- @param args {table} -- @return {mw.html table} -- local function footer( tbl, args ) local th = insertRow( tbl ) :tag( 'th' ) :attr( 'colspan', '2' ) :addClass( 'navbox-footer' )
if args.fstyle then th:cssText( args.fstyle ) end
if mw.ustring.match( args.footer, '^%s*%*' ) then th:newline()
-- trim whitespace on bullets local spl = mw.text.split( args.footer, '\n' )
for i = 1, #spl do spl[i] = mw.text.trim( spl[i] ) end
args.footer = table.concat( spl, '\n' )
th:addClass( 'navbox-list' ) end
th:wikitext( args.footer )
return th:allDone() end
-- -- Adds [[Category:Navbox templates]] to navbox template pages -- -- @return {string} -- local function categories() local title = mw.title.getCurrentTitle() local page = title.text local ns = title.nsText
if ns == 'Template' then -- sort in category by pagename return '[[Category:Navbox templates| ' .. page .. ']]' else return '' end
end
-- -- Adds [[Template:Navbox/doc]] to navbox template pages -- -- @param args {table} -- @return {string} -- local function docs( args ) local frame = mw.getCurrentFrame() local title = mw.title.getCurrentTitle() local base = title.baseText local ns = title.nsText
-- not if a subpage of [[Template:Navbox]] if base ~= 'Navbox' and -- in template ns ns == 'Template' and -- not a navbox group within a navbox not yesno(args.subgroup, false) and -- not a collapsible navbox within a navbox not yesno(args.collapsible, false) and -- not if the doc argument is not set to "yes" yesno(args.doc, false) then return frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Navbox/doc' } else return '' end
end
-- -- Navbox method to allow it to be called by other modules -- -- @param _args {table} -- @return {string} -- function p._navbox( _args ) local args = {} local wkCss = '' local wkDiv = '' local j
-- preserves parser function behaviour where an empty string is considered undefined -- or nil in lua's case for k, v in pairs( _args ) do if v ~= '' then args[k] = v end end
local tbl = createTbl( args )
if not yesno(args.subgroup, false) then tbl = header( tbl, args ) end
-- insert up to 25 rows for i = 1, 25 do j = tostring( i )
if args['group' .. j] then tbl = row( tbl, args['gtitle' .. j], args['group' .. j], args['gtype' .. j], args['style' .. j], args.name, args.subgroup ) else break end end
if args.footer then tbl = footer( tbl, args ) end
tbl = tostring( tbl )
local cats = '' if not yesno(args.subgroup, false) and not yesno(args.hidecat, false) then cats = categories() end local docs = docs( args )
return tbl .. cats .. docs end
-- -- Main navbox method accessed through #invoke -- -- @param frame {table} -- @return {string} -- function p.navbox( frame ) local args = frame:getParent().args return p._navbox( args ) end
return p -- </nowiki>

-- <nowiki> -- -- Implements {{tnavbar}} and variants -- -- @todo move the hardcoded css to [[MediaWiki:Common.css]] given how many pages it's found on -- require('strict') local p = {} local yesno = require( 'Module:Yesno' )
function p._navbar( args ) local navbarstyle = args.style or '' local fontstyle = args.fontstyle or '' local view, talk, edit = (args.view or true), (args.talk or true), (args.edit or true)
local desc = { view = 'view', talk = 'talk', edit = 'edit' }
local ret = mw.html.create( 'div' ) :addClass( 'navbar' ) :addClass( 'inline' ) :addClass( 'plainlinks' ) :addClass( 'hlist' ) :addClass( 'noprint' ) :css( { ['white-space'] = 'nowrap', ['font-weight'] = 'normal', ['font-size'] = 'x-small' } ) :cssText( navbarstyle )
if yesno( args.mini ) then desc = { view = 'v', talk = 't', edit = 'e' } ret:addClass( 'navbar-mini' ) end
local viewSpan = mw.html.create( 'span' ) :attr( 'title', 'View this template' ) :cssText( fontstyle ) :wikitext( desc.view )
local talkSpan = mw.html.create( 'span' ) :attr( 'title', 'Discussion about this template' ) :cssText( fontstyle ) :wikitext( desc.talk )
local editSpan = mw.html.create( 'span' ) :attr( 'title', 'Edit this template' ) :cssText( fontstyle ) :wikitext( desc.edit )
local title = args[1] and mw.text.trim( args[1] ) or error('No page title given') local ns, titleTbl, pagelink, talklink
if mw.ustring.sub( title, 1, 1 ) == ':' then -- mainspace title = mw.ustring.sub( title, 2 ) pagelink = title talklink = 'Talk:' .. title
elseif mw.ustring.match( title, ':' ) then -- split title to see if it has a valid namespace titleTbl = mw.text.split( title, ':' ) ns = mw.site.namespaces[titleTbl[1]]
if ns ~= nil then pagelink = ns.name .. ':' .. table.concat( titleTbl, '', 2 )
if ns.isTalk then talklink = page else talklink = ns.talk.name .. ':' .. table.concat( titleTbl, '', 2 ) end end end
-- this happens if there's no semi-colons in title -- or if there is semi-colons but it didn't have valid ns name if not pagelink then pagelink = 'Template:' .. title talklink = 'Template talk:' .. title end
local ul = ret:tag('ul') local function listgen(link, protection) local li = ul:tag('li'):wikitext( link ) if (protection == 'autoconfirmed') then li:addClass( 'autoconfirmed-show' ):css( 'display', 'none' ) end li:done() end
listgen( '[[' .. pagelink .. '|' .. tostring( viewSpan ) .. ']]' ) -- v listgen( '[' .. tostring( mw.uri.fullUrl( talklink ) ) .. ' ' .. tostring( talkSpan ) .. ']', 'autoconfirmed' ) -- t listgen( '[[Special:EditPage/' .. pagelink .. '|' .. tostring( editSpan ) .. ']]' ) -- e ret:allDone()
if yesno( args.brackets ) then ret = '[ ' .. tostring( ret ) .. ' ]' else ret = tostring( ret ) end
return ret end
function p.navbar( frame ) return p._navbar( frame:getParent().args ) end
return p
